articleTitle: Research on pedestrian vehicle collision warning based on path prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The vehicle FCW (forward collision warning) system is supposed to considerable reduce the traffic accidents caused by pedestrian crossing. The pedestrian path prediction method in FCW is studied, and the five-freedom-degree vehicle model is analyzed, the limit condition where whether the maximum barking acceleration can avoid collision effectively is researched. The vehicle coordinate is divided according to the psychological safety distance of pedestrians, and an anti-collision warning system is designed on basis of the pedestrian initial position, the movement speed and path. The test results show that the designed anti-collision warning system can effectively warn the driver before the collision accident occurs and avoid pedestrian traffic accidents caused by the negligence of the drivers.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Dual-channel Active Control Method for Transverse Vibration of Ship Propulsion Shaft System
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The ship propulsion shaft system is an indispensable power component of the ship, and its stability and reliability are crucial to the safety of the ship. The transverse vibration of the ship’s shaft system in the operating condition is a serious threat to the safety of ship operation. Therefore, it is of great engineering significance and research value to control the transverse vibration of ship propulsion shaft system and ship hull vibration control.Based on the vibration control theory, adaptive filtering and Fx-LMS algorithm, the active control scheme for transverse vibration of ship propulsion shaft system is studied, and the control scheme is optimized for the shortcomings. Finally, the effectiveness of the active control scheme of ship propulsion shaft system transverse vibration proposed in this paper is verified through the test.The research results show that the ship propulsion shaft system can effectively suppress the ship shaft system transverse vibration caused by propeller pulse excitation by adopting the active control scheme of transverse vibration proposed in this paper, which has a good control effect and provides a new technical reference for the ship shaft system transverse vibration control.

articleTitle: Risk Evolution Analysis of Maritime Traffic Accidents in Coastal Areas of China
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The study of water traffic accidents can help to understand the causes and mechanisms of water accidents, so as to help reduce the occurrence of water accidents and improve the level of maritime safety management. Based on the investigation report of China’s coastal water traffic accidents, this study analyzes the risk evolution of water traffic accidents based on accident causation theory and complex network theory, and discusses the risk evolution characteristics of China’s coastal water traffic accidents from the stages of accident latency, diffusion and occurrence in combination with network topology characteristics. The research results show that ship collision is the main accident type of coastal water traffic in my country, and improper operation and human error are the key causes of accidents; accident evolution has obvious characteristics such as short transmission path and strong randomness, and the risk factors are interdependent; many Node failures are more likely to cause the system to crash, resulting in accidents.

articleTitle: Perception of Causal Factors in Flight Operations Between Ab-Initio and Expatriate Pilots
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The establishment of objectives in organizational safety management systems (SMS) are dependent on how the workforce perceives hazards and deficiencies. In the Asia region, it is common for airlines to recruit pilots through both ab-initio cadet programs, as well as to hire experienced expatriates from predominantly Western countries. When the workforce contains a mix of cultures and training backgrounds, perceptual differences may affect the relevance of SMS objectives and the effectiveness of consequential safety interventions. The present research compared experienced airline pilots from Asian ab-initio backgrounds with their Western, expatriate counterparts on the attribution of safety conditions related to hierarchical relations, organizational faults, human performance limitations, external faults, and human-machine interface conflicts. It was discovered that cultural values on interpersonal relations, desire for guidance, and social distance to an ‘in-group’ influenced the classification of safety deficiencies. The findings encourage SMS practitioners to include a wider diversity of perspectives when carrying out organizational SMS processes.

articleTitle: Resilience Analysis of Container Port Networks based on Motif Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Disruptions in maritime shipping may cause significant burdens and damage to local and global businesses. Considering the increasing connections and dynamics in maritime port operations for global maritime shipping, it is important to study the resilience of port networks in order to better mitigate disruption risks. Considering the growing interconnections and dynamics in maritime port operations within the global maritime shipping industry, it becomes crucial to study the resilience of port networks. However, a lot of network research tends to focus on big-picture viewpoints, sometimes missing the hidden processes that make real-world networks resilient and able to bounce back from disruptions. Networks that look similar when viewed from a broad perspective can actually be quite different when zooming in on motifs, which are small sections of a network involving multiple nodes and often seen as a basic building block of networks. Hence, This paper presents a motif-based method for studying the resilience of container port networks. Unlike methods that only look at the overall network structure, focusing on motifs can help to better understand local network structures and how they function. Our method is applied to two representative container port networks, centered at two Southeast Asian ports, respectively, with the aim of acquiring insights that are useful in real-world operations.

articleTitle: A Cognitive Approach for Identification of Ship Illegal Behaviors by Using Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In order to improve the ability of refined management and service of ships, this paper uses the scientific Knowledge graph technology to build a ship Knowledge graph for ship illegal behaviors analysis. Based on the Knowledge graph of ships, this paper carries out the analysis of the characteristics of the map of ship violations in the jurisdiction, conducts intelligent identification for specific violations such as ship fake licensing, and develops a ship Knowledge graph decision-making system, Implement the verification application of ship profiling and identification of violations, effectively improve the level of maritime data application, and enhance maritime supervision and decision-making capabilities for ship safety.

articleTitle: Safety Risk Identification of Lithium-ion Battery Based on Kolmogorov Complexity
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Battery is the key component and main trouble source of an electric vehicle (EV). With the rapid growth of market share, thermal runaway caused by malfunction of batteries have been frequently reported, so fault diagnosis is critical to ensure safety and to improve performance. Unfortunately, most of the existing fault diagnosis methods only focus on the identification of voltage anomalies on single cell level, ignoring the characteristics on macro system level. Consequently, without obvious abnormality in voltage, faults of certain types can hardly be caught. This paper proposes a novel fault diagnosis method based on Kolmogorov complexity, which can quantitatively describe the degree of confusion over battery pack level to identify potential risk. The proposed method is verified by real EVs operation data collected through the National Monitoring and Management Center for New Energy Vehicles, where clear correlation between the increased level of Kolmogorov complexity and thermal runaway is observed. As a simple conclusion, the proposed method can be an important supplement to traditional fault diagnosis methods.

articleTitle: Safety assessment of hydrogen fuel cell powered ships during navigation
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The hydrogen fuel powered ship in navigation interacts with the surrounding ships, shore constructions and people. Therefore, it is necessary to assess the ship safety during navigation. This article selects the hydrogen fuel powered ship which will sailing in Yangtze River as research object to study the ship risks in navigation and assess the consequences of accidents. Jet flame accident and flash accident are two main accident scenarios that may occur during the sailing of hydrogen fuel cell powered ships. Based on the HyRAM software, the flame size, thermal radiation range and fatality rate of the ship under these two scenarios are quantitatively analyzed, and the sailing risk of the ship is quantitatively assessed. The risks of the hydrogen fuel powered ship in navigation is evaluated quantitatively by calculating the personal risk and determine the risks which can be accepted by crew, passengers on board and people on shore.

articleTitle: The Regional Protocol for Local Communications Among Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships Based on VDES
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In order to provide more collision avoidance information to ships that may encounter each other in dense sea areas, prevent collision events, and minimize channel data pressure, ensure network reliability and reduce latency, this paper proposes a regional protocol for local communications among maritime autonomous surface ships based on VDES (High Frequency Data Exchange System). Based on the theoretical foundation of the ship domain model in the field of ships, the area where collision danger exists is found by guiding the ship domain model, and this area is used as the routing flood area, and the routing request is limited to this area. The improved AODV (Ad hoc On-Demand Distance Vector) routing forwarding algorithm is used to establish a communication link between ships in the routing request area using real-time location information. This can exchange more information with ships located in the collision risk area to assist in collaborative obstacle avoidance and prevent accidents. At the same time, it effectively avoids network-wide routing flooding, avoids network congestion, and ensures network stability. Simulation analysis shows that this protocol is superior to AIS in terms of delivery rate and delay on the basis of realizing business functions. This will be beneficial for obstacle avoidance between encountering ships.

articleTitle: A Method of Analyzing Flight Exceedance Events Based on Association Rule and QAR Data
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Flight Operation Quality Assurance (FOQA) is a crucial approach to improve safety by monitoring exceedance events. However, an exceedance event implies the monitoring parameters of flight data exceed the standard, and is determined by multiple causes such as pilots’ operations and environmental conditions. In order to provide support for the judgment of pilots’ exceedance behaviors, this paper utilized the Apriori algorithm to mine association rules in exceedance events and their correlations with environmental conditions (e.g., season and airport). Results revealed some critical associations, such as the speed exceedance during approach at an altitude of 500-50ft is more likely to result in speed exceedance during approach at an altitude below 50ft. Our findings are expected to help airlines consider exceedance events more reasonably, as well as identify the environmental factors associated with exceedance events.

articleTitle: AGV path planning and optimization with deep reinforcement learning model
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The rapid progress in global port construction has resulted in a significant rise in container throughput. As the development of automated container terminals continues, it is imperative to enhance the intelligence and environmental friendliness of Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs). This paper focuses on addressing the AGV path planning problem by employing deep reinforcement learning. The primary objectives are to optimize data collection efficiency and minimize battery consumption. The diverse layouts of terminal environments are represented using RGB images, and path learning is incorporated with a meticulously designed reward function. Here, we perform 1000 simulations using Monte Carlo to evaluate the parameters for these four scenarios. The evaluation showed that the terminal path planning battery consumption averaged around 40 to 56, the data collection rates were all above 80% on average, and more than 99% of them resulted in optimal solutions in a 32×32 size environment. The algorithm is able to reach and collect the data as fast as possible.

articleTitle: Drivers’ Heart Rate Variability Analysis under Different Tunnel Cross-section Designs: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: As a special component of the highway traffic facilities, the tunnel could might affect drivers’ physiology because of the limited space. Although the highway tunnel design guidelines are met, the different cross-section designs would have different effects on drivers. The aim of this study was to analyze the drivers’ physiology difference when driving in two tunnels with different cross-section designs. The two different tunnel cross-section designs had the same tunnel construction clearance. One of the design has an arc-shaped top, and the other is almost rectangular. Hence, a driving simulator study was conducted and drivers’ heart rate variability (HRV) data were collected and analyzed. It was found that (1) for the passenger car drivers, who have a lower viewpoint, their HRV data had no significant difference; (2) for the commercial vehicle drivers, who have a higher viewpoint, the AVNN indicator showed significant differences.

articleTitle: Design of Torque angle based photoelectric shaft power acquisition device and data processing method
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Ship shaft power is one of the important performance parameters in the ship’s power system, and the real-time working condition of the ship can be effectively evaluated by monitoring the change of shaft power in real time. Therefore, the measurement of shaft power has a very important research value in the field of ships. Photoelectric shaft power has the advantages of simple structure and small size, and has a very wide range of applications in the field of ships. Based on the principle of phase difference measurement, this paper independently designs a set of photoelectric non-contact shaft power device, including the design of photoelectric code disc, photoelectric sensor and main control system. Through photoelectric detection method, the phase difference of two pulse signals is obtained, and then the Torque Angle is measured, and then the torque under the current state can be calculated according to the change of the Torque Angle. Due to the processing and installation errors of the photoelectric code disc, the data of the rotating shaft under measurement fluctuates greatly, which requires filtering. In this paper, the periodic errors caused by the processing and installation of the photoelectric code disc will be reduced by the sliding window algorithm method. Finally, the experimental platform was built and the comparison device was installed to compare and verify the measurement results of the photoelectric shaft power device.

articleTitle: Study on Optimization and characteristics of Ship-based carbon capture System based on intercooling Process
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Ship-based carbon capture (SBCC) and storage technology is an effective way to realize the and emission reduction of ships and the greening of the shipping industry. In order to solve the problems of low decarbonization rate and high energy consumption issues of SBCC systems, a carbon capture model of LNG ship exhaust gas with a 3MW main engine was constructed based on ASPEN PLUS. Optimized basic process including absorber tower packing height, stripper diameter, and absorption liquid concentration process parameters were 9m, 0.74m, and 37.5%, respectively. The intercooling process was added to further improve the system decarbonization rate, and an orthogonal text was designed to explore the ideal installation parameter of intercooler. The intercool load, location, and temperature were 70%, 18, and 10°C, respectively. The advantages and disadvantages of the carbon capture capacity of the two technologies were analyzed from the aspects of solvent flow ratio and reflux ratio. It was proved that at the same processing conditions, the carbon capture amount of intercooling process was always higher than that of basic process. Adjusted solvent flow ratio intercooling process was 6.60% higher than the base process, solvent usage was reduced by 12.27%. articleTitle: Improving energy efficiency of ships by modifying hull surface via coating Cu NPs *
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Antifouling is an important research challenge in marine tribology. Since ships are permanently exposed to an aqueous environment, their hulls are prone to fouling. With the increase of time, the ship hull surface will be covered by a dense layer of firmly attaching organisms such as barnacles, mussels and seaweeds. These layers strongly increase the drag and reduce the fuel efficiency. Copper nanoparticles possess excellent antifouling performance. In this study, in situ generation of Cu NPs on the surface of dopamine modified 304 stainless steel in weak alkaline aqueous solution was reported. Field emission scanning electron microscope, contact angle measurement and x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy were utilized to analyze the chemical composition and surface wettability of the modified stainless steel. The results demonstrated that the surface of stainless steel was coated with polydopamine and Cu NPs successfully. Antibacterial assay showed that modified surface possessed the ability of resistance of Vibrio natriegens. The presence of copper offers the coatings excellent capability to inhibit effectively the adhesion of marine algae Phaeodactylum tricornutum. This strategy exhibited a realistic paradigm for further improving the antifouling performances of hull surfaces.

articleTitle: Study on real-time collision avoidance decision-making under 5G environment
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of real-time collision prevention and untimely early warning, an intelligence infrastructure which based on 5G and Beidou is constructed. The real-time data collection of Beidou and AIS is used for preprocessing and filling, which improves the accuracy and usability of Beidou and AIS data, and provides a reliable data source for the real-time collision risk assessment of ships. By establishing distance to closest point of approach (DCPA) model and Time to closest point of approach (TCPA) model, the collision risk of ships in space and in time domain are obtained, and then real-time navigation collision risk index (CRI) are obtained, the safety warning of ships with different risk levels is realized by CRI. Taking Nanjing Banqiao ferry as a demonstration point, the DCPA model and TCPA model were applied to the ferry safety management system, multiple real-time warnings are carried out, and the early warning accuracy rate was up to 96.15%, which was unanimously praised by the management department. Finally, the factors to be considered for subsequent optimization of the CRI model are pointed out.

articleTitle: Identification of engine order telegraph operational error based on image and speech recognition technologies
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The unsafe steering behaviors(USBs) of the crew are the main causes of navigational accidents. Accurate and timely identification of the crew 's USBs contributes to preventing and reducing the occurrence of navigational accidents. This paper proposed a machine learning method for recognizing the USBs while using engine order telegraph in manual steering mode. The standard engine order given by the captain or pilot is recognized by automatic speech recognition technology, and the status of speedometer is recognized using image recognition technology to evaluate whether the behavior and the order matches. Experiment using navigational simulator is carried to verify the accuracy of the method. The results show that the method can contribute to rapid response and recovery from operational errors, which in turn improve navigational safety.

articleTitle: Ship collision avoidance method in starboard-to-starboard head-on situations
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Among maritime incidents, ship collision accidents account for the majority. According to the report by International Maritime Organization, more than 80 percent of maritime accidents are attributed to inappropriate decisions due to the misunderstanding of the situations or the instructions by International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea (COLREGs). Due to the complexity and variability of encounter situations, officers on board may have different understandings, and the resulting actions will also be different. Among the three encounter situations, the collision avoidance responsibility in crossing and overtaking situations is identified by defining stand-on and give-way ships. But in head-on situations, two ships share equal avoidance responsibility, i.e., both should take appropriate actions. Therefore, the coordination of the actions is crucial. As required by COLREGs, both ships turn starboard side. In port-to-port situations, such actions enlarge the distance and probably lead to the goal. However, in starboard-to-starboard situations, such actions may even cause a closer distance and a higher risk of collision. In this paper, Deep Q Network is adopted to solve the collision avoidance problem of two ships in starboard-to-starboard head-on situations. By setting different initial ship speed and different initial distances, the encounter scenarios are depicted in detail. Based on the instructions by COLREGs and the navigational experience, the set of collision avoidance actions and the reward functions are proposed, to determine the optimal collision avoidance actions of ships in specific situations. Besides, the coordination between the ships is also considered. The research results provide theoretical references for the autonomous collision avoidance scheme of ships in specific scenarios and can be applied to practical ship collision avoidance in the transition period from fully manned ships to intelligent unmanned ships.

articleTitle: Exploring the Utilization of a Bayesian Network-Based Risk Management System for Cold Chain Packaging
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive risk management model for cold chain packaging, as there is still a lack of systematic approaches to address this industry-wide issue. The proposed Bayesian network model is based on literature review and expert opinions of existing cold chain packaging systems to identify various risks and factors. The model includes various components related to the cold chain packaging system. This model can be used by stakeholders such as logistic managers and consultants to weigh the impact of each risk factor and identify potential risks that may affect the effectiveness of the cold chain system. In addition, the model can be used to evaluate the overall effectiveness of the cold chain system and suggest ways to further improve the system. The model will provide valuable insights for industry practitioners to better plan and manage cold chain packaging operations.

articleTitle: An Improved Detection Method of Traffic Prohibition Sign for Intelligent Vehicles based on YOLOV5s
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Traffic sign detection and recognition is an important task in the perception of intelligent vehicles (IVs). Among various categories of traffic signs, prohibition signs are of paramount importance. However, there is relatively little research on the detection and recognition of prohibition signs at present. In this study, a modified lightweight model based on YOLOV5s is proposed for detecting the 12 most common types of Chinese prohibition signs. A new dataset is established by collecting images of Chinese prohibition traffic signs in real-world scenarios. The improved model replaces the normal convolution with ghost convolution in the feature fusion network, which greatly reduces the number of parameters and computational complexity. The introduction of the coordinate attention mechanism in the feature extraction network helps the network to better learn and leverage the position information of the target on the feature map. The Mosaic data augmentation strategy at the input end is refined by increasing the number of concatenated images from 4 to 9, allowing the network to learn a richer representation of the scene and target features. The experimental results on the self-built dataset demonstrate that the proposed algorithm, compared to YOLOV5s, achieves a significant reduction in model parameters of 28.4%, model size of 27.5%, and computational cost of 27% while only experiencing a slight decrease in accuracy of 0.3%. Further comparative experiment results show that compared with current mainstream lightweight algorithms, our proposed model achieves a better balance between lightweight and accuracy.

articleTitle: Quantitative Study on Wear of Water-Lubricated Bearings in Sediment Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Water-lubricated bearings are widely used in propulsion shafting of large marine equipment, such as ships. When a water-lubricated stern bearing operates in harsh environments involving a low speed and heavy load for extended periods, there is a serious impact on the friction and wear performance of the bearing. In this study, a full pair of bearings made of a special polymer material was used as the research object in a sediment environment and was subjected to low-speed heavy-duty durability tests. At different temperatures, specific pressures, and speed conditions, the friction coefficient and wear were measured and linearly extrapolated. The results show that under harsh working conditions such as low speed and heavy load sediment, and the loading pressure is greater. It is difficult to form a complete water film between the friction pairs. A loading pressure of 0.2 MPa is beneficial to the long-term operation of the bearing under harsh working conditions. Moreover, the bearing damage is not serious, resulting in a reduction in bearing wear and an extension of operation life.

articleTitle: Parameter optimization of supercritical CO2 Brayton cycle for flue gas waste heat recovery of Marine high-speed diesel engine
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: With the high-speed diesel engine test data of the flue gas as the initial conditions and the boundaries, the arrangement of the S-CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> recompression Brayton cycle (SCRBC) is established and the optimization of the S-CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> Brayton cycle (SCBC) system for CHD622V20 diesel engine are studied. Additionally, the model accuracy has been validated with the test data from Sandia National Laboratories (SNL). Finally, the feasibility of the SCBC applied in flue gas waste heat recovery (WHR) for marine engines is comprehensively assessed from the efficiency, the net output power, the fuel consumed rate and the exergy. The results show that with the recompression Brayton cycle layout in the optimal configuration, the high-speed marine diesel engine could reach 1.00% of the maximum total efficiency improvement and 5.58 g/kW$\cdot $h of the fuel consumed rate reduction at 25% load, the maximum net output power increased to 21.54 kW. The cooler, flue gas heat exchanger and high-temperature recuperator (HTR) modules are the weak points of the SCRBC system through the exergy analysis, and further optimization of the SCRBC system should first focus on improving these components.

articleTitle: Urban transportation network resilience assessment based on entropy weight method and GMM clustering algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In this paper, an urban transportation network resilience evaluation method based on entropy weight method and Gaussian mixture model (GMM) clustering algorithm is proposed. Firstly, based on the topological characteristic variables of complex network theory and the characteristic variables describing traffic operation, the topological and traffic class evaluation index system affecting the resilience of urban traffic road network is constructed, followed by the calculation of information entropy by the entropy weight method to determine the weight of each index and establish a comprehensive evaluation model of resilience by this method. Finally, the transportation system was constructed with Sioux Falls city as an example, and the resilience index of this traffic road network was calculated, and the results were input into the GMM clustering algorithm to evaluate the road resilience level.

articleTitle: Collaboration Scheme for Multi-ship Collision Avoidance using Available Maneuvering Margin
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Autonomous collision avoidance has received numerous attentions in recent years due to the focus on Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS). As a result, many algorithms have been developed for collision avoidance (CA), and Velocity Obstacle (VO) algorithm or Collision Threat Parameter Area (CTPA) is one popular algorithm for CA in recent years due to its simple form and low communication burden. However, since it does not consider global information, the VO algorithm might lead to deadlocks in congested waters. To solve this problem, a distributed collaboration scheme for multi-ship collision avoidance is proposed. The ships are assumed to share their navigation information including their possible trajectories in the future. Then, each ship calculates its Available Maneuvering Margin (AMM) at present, a potential collision-free course using the VO algorithm, and the expected AMM adopting the collision-free course. Based on the differences between the expected AMM and the original AMM, the priorities of taking evasive actions are determined. By utilizing AMM-ascending and AMM-descending orders to determine the decision-making sequence of ships, the probability of deadlock occurrence can be reduced. To demonstrate the proposed collaboration scheme, some experiments are introduced, and the performance of the original VO algorithm and the VO with the proposed collaboration scheme are compared. The proposed scheme is expected to reduce the deadlock using the original VO algorithm and reduce the communication burden in multi-ship collaborative collision avoidance, which would improve the safety and efficiency of shipping in congested waters.

articleTitle: Study on Minimum Tangent Length of Identical Direction in Expressway Reconstruction and Expansion through Driving Behavior
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The expressway reconstruction and expansion project is influenced by various factors such as terrain and engineering volume. As a result, it often needs to be rebuilt based on the existing road. Due to the limited range of route adjustment, it can be challenging to meet all the requirements of current design speed specifications.A study was conducted to determine the minimum tangent length for safe driving during expressway reconstruction and expansion projects. Driving simulations were used to analyze driver perception with different straight line lengths between curves of the same direction. Six evaluation indicators were used to assess mental load: recognition level, physical strength level, time level, effort level, satisfaction level, and boredom level. By considering these indicators, researchers determined the optimal tangent length that minimizes mental load while ensuring safe driving conditions.In addition to simulation experiments, on-site observations and analysis were conducted for the reconstruction and expansion project of Shenshan West Expressway. Traffic flow monitoring was carried out on typical short straight road sections to evaluate their impact on vehicle following and traffic accident risk. Various traffic flow safety indicators such as DHW (Deceleration Headway), THW (Time Headway), TTC (Time-to-Collision), PICUD (Post-Incident Car Unit Distance), and DRAC (Driver Reaction Time After Collision) were analyzed to understand the specific effects of short straight road sections on traffic safety.Based on the analysis results, it was determined that a straight line length of 4V between curves in the same direction is sufficient to meet the driving requirements of drivers in expressway reconstruction and expansion projects. This finding provides valuable insights for highway design professionals in optimizing road geometry and ensuring safe driving conditions for motorists.

articleTitle: The CFD-DEM coupled numerical simulation for the oil spill in ice-covered waters
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The Arctic region is rich in oil and gas reserves, accounting for 25% of the world’s untapped oil resources. With the increase of oil transportation activities in the region, the risk of oil spills from ships has increased. The external environment encountered by ships operating in ice areas is mainly a coupled system of sea ice with wind, waves, and currents. For the numerical simulation of this coupled system, a numerical ice pool is established in this paper using the coupled CFD-DEM method. Specifically, a physical sea ice model is established using the discrete element method. Then a 3D pool is established based on the VOF model, and the two are coupled and calculated through the CFD-DEM interface to realize the simulation effect of the numerical ice pool. Finally, the oil spill diffusion law under different sea ice concentrations, oil spill velocity, and current velocity is analyzed by adding the ship oil spill, which provides the decision basis for the ship oil spill emergency treatment. Through numerical experiments, it is found that the averaged flow velocity has a greater influence on oil spill diffusion, and the oil spill speed has a smaller influence on diffusion. When the sea ice concentration is located at 30-50%, sea ice has a certain obstruction to oil spill diffusion in more open waters, and when the sea ice concentration is greater than 80%, the obstruction effect is obvious, and when the sea ice concentration is 100%, the oil spill diffuses on the lower surface of sea ice.

articleTitle: Reliability and Validity on Influencing Factors of Pilot Chronic Stress
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Since pilot stress has received much more attention in civil aviation, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic, this study aimed to explore the influencing factors of pilot chronic stress. First, we reviewed the relevant studies and compiled the initial "Influencing Factors of Pilot Chronic Stress Scale" (IFPCSS). Then, we invited 202 professional pilots from a Chinese airline to rate their feeling on it, with 189 valid responses received. Further, the study calculated the validity using Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) and Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA). Ultimately, we evaluated Cronbach’s alpha to analyze the internal consistency. As a result, EFA revealed that the optimized IFPCSS can be divided into three dimensions with 12 items. CFA confirmed that the final IFPCSS was acceptable since Cronbach’s alpha was 0.899, which indicated good internal reliability.

articleTitle: Abnormal Behavior Detection and Risk Analysis of Ships in the Yangtze River Estuary
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The Yangtze River Estuary is one of the shipping hubs in China. In order to ensure the safety of ship navigation, it is necessary to study the detection of abnormal behavior of ships. In this paper, the abnormal behavior of ships is identified through the study of ship behavior, and the potential accident risk factors are analyzed. Firstly, the route is identified by trajectory compression and clustering algorithm. Then, according to the distribution of the ship’s lateral position, the abnormal behavior of the ship’s offset is detected. Finally, the risk model is established by using the dynamic Bayesian network, and the influence of the detected abnormal behavior on the potential accident risk is analyzed. According to the AIS data of ships in the Yangtze River Estuary of China, it is found that the Nangang Shuidao of the Yangtze River Estuary is prone to the risk of abnormal behavior of ships. The results show that the course over ground and ship heading have a great influence on the risk of the abnormal behavior of the ship’s lateral deviation, and the improper control of the ship’s speed causes the abnormal behavior of the ship’s lateral deviation.

articleTitle: Time-based Resilience Enhancement with Dual Berth Allocation Strategies in Bulk Cargo Terminals under Machinery Failure Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In bulk cargo terminals, machinery failures during vessel berthing operations inevitably disrupt the normal loading and unloading processes. The berth allocation process in such terminals encompasses numerous failure scenarios, with variations in the timing and severity of machinery malfunctions, resulting in numerous operational challenges for vessels. To tackle these problems, this study investigates two recovery strategies aimed at modifying the existing berth allocation plans. The research focuses on enhancing the time-based resilience metric, considering the diverse scenarios of machinery failures in bulk cargo terminals. By implementing dual-strategy recovery approaches, this study aims to mitigate the impact of machinery failures on vessel operations and optimize the berth allocation process. The findings of this research contribute to the development of effective strategies for minimizing disruptions and improving the overall operational efficiency of bulk cargo terminals.

articleTitle: Simulation-driven multi-segment variable speed limits on freeway
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Variable Speed Limits (VSL) have great potential for increasing freeway traffic efficiency. This paper presents a multi-segment lane-level VSL system, in which speed limits of each lane can be adjusted respectively. In addition, a simulation-driven method is proposed to test and analyze different VSL strategies with respect of speed, occupancy and travel time. The simulation-driven method is based on the SUMO simulator and traffic control interface. Different commands can be applied to adjust speed limits of edges and lanes. The results show that multi-segment lane-level VSL strategies can significantly improve traffic efficiency. This approach can be applied to a long-distance freeway section with multiple variable message signs.

articleTitle: A framework for the use of big data in the emergency response supply chain1
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: This paper sets out a framework for use in the overlapping fields of the emergency response supply chain and big data analytics. The framework comprises four dimensions. The first dimension relates to the useful purpose of big data analytics: descriptive, diagnostic, predictive and prescriptive. The second dimension relates the phase of the emergency or disaster within which the analytics are used: preparation, preparation, response or recovery. The third dimension relates to the characteristics of big data itself: volume, variety, velocity, veracity and value. The fourth dimension relates to the application area. While the following four areas have been identified from the literature it is likely that additional areas will evolve: logistics, social media, remote sensing and security. It is intended that this conceptual framework will be of use to researchers and practitioners in positioning their work in the field.

articleTitle: Characteristics and correlation analysis of fog distribution in the upper Yangtze River waterways
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Based on the field observations of fog distribution from 1954-2015 at the upper reaches of the Yangtze River, the Mann-Kendall (M-K) and the Moving TTest (MTT) mutation detection methods have been applied to study the characteristics of annually averaged fog days as well as revealing the mutation patterns and period. The occurrence patterns of extreme weather conditions in the research domain were also explored and discussed. The correlation analysis between the fog characteristics and the precipitation, freight volume, port cargo throughput, hydrological conditions indicate that mutation changes of fog conditions in the Chongqing reach shows a clear pattern with short cycles of 8a,16a and long cycles of 20a, 32a. The temporal mutation changes are consistent with the occurrence of regional climatic extreme such as high temperatures and precipitation. The variation of fog distribution has a correlation with the seasonal precipitation and hydrological conditions, positive in spring and summer, negative in autumn. However, the correlation during the winter is not significant. The kappa consistency test indicates that the freight volume was also affected by the fog condition, cause its significance value(P) and kappa value are 0.024, -0.238. Cargo turnover and port cargo throughput are 0.983, 0.309 in P, 0.003, -0.128 in kappa respectively. It is concluded that both cargo turnover and port cargo are not related to annually fog days significantly.

articleTitle: Vibration Characteristics of Additive Manufactured IWP-type TPMS Gradient Lattice Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Lattice structures combined with light weight and better mechanical properties are widely used in the marine and aerospace industries. Therefore, the triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) lattice structure is chosen as the object of study in this paper. Since there are few studies on the vibration of such structures, the vibration-related properties were investigated by designing positive and negative gradient volume fraction TPMS structures in conjunction with the gradient concept. The sweep and vibration tests show that the designed IWP-type structure can provide vibration isolation in the low frequency range. At resonance the positive gradient structure has a higher resonant frequency due to its higher stiffness, but the negative gradient structure has a higher damping ratio and a wide frequency isolation band gap.

articleTitle: Study of Ships Safety Smart Monitoring System in Inland Restricted Water Area
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Presently, the ultra-high detection of ships technical approaches includes Automatic Identification System(AIS) with laser radar, infrared imaging, laser altimeter and infrared laser. However, these ultra-high detection technical approaches are not perfect, resulting in cost high, application range small and false alarm rate high. In this study, a ships safety smart monitoring system which is low false alarm, high reliability and automatic detection, is proposed to detect the ultra-high ships in inland restricted water area. Firstly, the performance of various ultra-high detection technologies is comparison and analysis. Secondly, a hardware platform of the ships safety smart monitoring system composed of system trigger module, ultra-high detection module, information processing module, alarm module and forensics module is constructed. Thirdly, the work flow and functions of the system are detailedly discussed. Next, the safety monitoring system in inland restricted water area has been proved in the pilot of Hai’an, the pilot shows that the system is able to improve economy, application range and data accuracy of detection. Finally, two factors which are improved are proposed, in order to indicate a direction for the following research.

articleTitle: Research on Data Resource Classification for Intelligent Highway Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In the realm of intelligent highways, vast amounts of data are generated from the activities involving with road design, construction, and management. These data require comprehensive collection, organization, and reconfiguration in order to form standardized and cohesive datasets that can be classified and graded for applications in intelligent scenarios, such as advanced driver assistance and intelligent road maintenance. The objective of this paper is to build a dataset that is replete with professional and detailed information for the applications of intelligent highway scenarios. For this purpose, an unified data resource directory is established, and highway data are classified through digital processing of various road engineering periods, including survey, design, construction, and maintenance. In the directory, each data element is accompanied by detailed information, including the name, source, content, format, etc. This information is more detailed and comprehensive than that of other existing information resource standards. Furthermore, a new type of data called “virtual space-time information” has been investigated and gathered. This type of data is specific originating from intelligent highway technical scenarios and is used to combine the dynamic and static data generated from massive traffic infrastructures and traffic operation status. By leveraging artificial intelligence, big data, cloud computing, and other technologies to simulate highway information, the data resource can ultimately serve as the foundation for various application scenarios such as construction supervision, maintenance analysis, and decision-making. Based on the aforementioned work, a method for classifying data into detailed categories has been devised, enabling different types of highway data to be categorized into groups and form an unified data resource. This resource can serve as a foundation and crucial support for intelligent highways.

articleTitle: Research on the Speed Planning Algorithm of Intelligent Mine Vehicle Based on Improved S-shaped Curve
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Speed planning is a crucial aspect of intelligent mine vehicle systems. To address the issue of low operational efficiency caused by the uniform speed scheme, a novel approach is proposed. Firstly, an adaptive speed processing method is introduced, considering factors such as vehicle speed limits and road curvature. Then, a fuzzy control method is used to determine the maximum acceleration limit for speed regulation, taking into account road slope and vehicle load. Furthermore, the S-curve method is innovatively applied to vehicle speed planning, with optimization of the traditional seven-segment S-curve to enhance computational efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate a 22.93% improvement in the working efficiency of the mine vehicle compared to traditional uniform speed driving. Additionally, the planned velocity curve exhibits superior stability and smoothness compared to the traditional trapezoidal velocity planning approach.

articleTitle: Analysis of injury severity in freeway and non-freeway crashes based on logit model and machine learning
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: This study applies the random parameter logit model (RPL), random parameter logit model with mean and variance heterogeneity (RPLMV), random forest (RF), and extreme random tree (ERT) to investigate the factors influencing the severity of both freeway and non-freeway crashes. Furthermore, it aims to analyze the disparities between logit models and tree-based machine learning models in terms of their predictive performance and interpretability. The findings of this research contribute to a better comprehension of the disparities in prediction accuracy and interpretive capabilities between logit models and machine learning models. Moreover, they provide insights into the selection and application of computational SHAP methods. Additionally, the outcomes can serve as valuable references for governmental bodies and organizations in formulating policies.

articleTitle: Risk assessment of steam cloud explosion and pool fire on water barge-type liquefied natural gas filling station
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: To assess the safety risks and damage levels of the liquefied natural gas filling station, steam cloud explosion and pool fire explosion are analyzed simulatedly. The results indicated that the radius of death, serious injury, minor injury and property loss in steam cloud explosion is 59.6 meters, 109.4 meters, 196.9 meters and 172.5 meters respectively. Then, in pool fire explosion, compared with the free expansion situation, the radius of death, serious injury and minor injury in the cofferdam containment situation is reduced by 145.4 meters, 178 meters and 253.5 meters respectively. Therefore, the research results showed that strengthening the cofferdam work can play a positive role in the safety maintenance of the water barge liquefied natural gas filling station.

articleTitle: Association Tracking of Vessels Using X-Band Radar Data in Complex Waterborne Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Accurate association tracking of targets in complex waterborne environment is a hot research topic in the field of waterborne transportation safety. In recent years, the number of vessels has steadily increased and the navigation environment of inland rivers has become increasingly crowded, which makes the existing association tracking method based on single radar echo feature information unable to achieve accurate association tracking of vessels in dense target scenarios. In order to solve the problem, a target association tracking method based on radar echo multi-feature information is proposed in this paper, which realizes the accurate association tracking of targets in dense target waterborne scenarios. Meanwhile, the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed method are verified by real radar data in the Jiangsu section of the Yangtze River.

articleTitle: Risk Identification Analysis of Fire Accidents for Passenger Ships by FMEA
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Fire accidents on passenger ships are frequent worldwide. This kind of accident has the characteristics of suddenness, rapid fire spread, and difficulty in evacuating passengers, which pose significant risks to personnel safety. This paper focuses on risk identification analysis of fire accidents on passenger ships using failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), based on the global maritime accident investigation reports of fire accidents for passenger ships from 11 maritime investigation agencies. First, we identify the accident scenarios of fire accidents in passenger ships from cabin fire, living compartment fire, and cargo compartment fire. Second, the equipment and its combustible materials that caused the fire in each scenario are identified. The failure mode of the equipment is obtained by focusing on the equipment that caused the greater risk of fire for a comprehensive analysis through the structure, equipment, process flow, and other related information in each fire accident scenario. Furthermore, the risk factors that cause fire accidents in each scenario are obtained by exploring each failure mode’s failure causes and effects. The research results can be used to propose risk control options for effectively reducing the risk of fire accidents on passenger ships.

articleTitle: The Jump Point Search algorithm based ship path planning in the Arctic environment
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The ship faces the challenge of complex sea ice conditions in the Arctic. To ensure safety and minimize the distance and search path time of the Arctic navigation, we propose an intelligent ship path planning method considering the influence of sea ice in the Arctic using the Jump Point Search (JPS) algorithm. The method dynamically evaluates the navigability from the POLARIS during path planning. The paths planned by JPS are the same length and quality as those planned by Dijkstra and A* algorithms. The number of searched nodes and the running time of the JPS algorithm are 0.03% of those of the Dijkstra algorithm. Furthermore, the JPS algorithm searches 2.68% of nodes searched in the A* algorithm and takes 0.31% of the time spent by the A* algorithm. The JPS algorithm has been justified as a suitable replacement for ship path planning in complex sea ice conditions of the conventional Dijkstra and A* algorithms in the Arctic.

Author Keywords: ship path planning in the Arctic

articleTitle: A Topology Based Path Planning Algorithm for Inland Waterway Network: Case Study of Jiangsu Canal Network
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Complex navigational conditions make it difficult for ship navigators to always generate safe and efficient paths in variable ship traffic flow, especially considering navigational constraints such as waterway grade, traffic congestion and lock nodes. This paper proposes a channel-based topology structure and establish a navigable waterway model in consideration of navigational constraints and lock nodes in inland waterway network. Moreover, an improved A-star algorithm based on channel topology is studied to achieve the shortest time path planning for the dynamic waterway network. Results from five case studies show that the proposed method outperforms both Dijkstra algorithm and traditional A-star algorithm in terms of computational efficiency and path generation.

articleTitle: A Novel Method of Automatic Ship Perception Based on the Information of PTZ Camera and Beidou Device in Wide Waters
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Traditional shore-based vision surveillance devices for wide waters can only track ships in a small area because current vision surveillance devices for wide waters usually use fixed-view cameras for sensing. In order to obtain a wider view, this paper proposes a vision-based ship sensing method that combines PTZ cameras with BeiDou devices to track ships accurately and robustly in wide waters. First, an active monitoring method based on PTZ camera is constructed to convert the pan and tilt angle of PTZ camera to the UTM coordinate of BeiDou device. In addition, to improve the tracking accuracy and robustness, a Kalman Filter-based ship tracking method is proposed to fuse the received BeiDou information with the positioning information of the PTZ camera to obtain more accurate ship position information. The proposed method and system have been validated in practical experiments. The results show that the system can accurately estimate the position of the ship at the next moment, while being able to actively track the automatic ship in a wide range of waters.

articleTitle: Constructing Waterborne Big Data Platform from the Perspective of Resilient Transportation
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Based on the latest research progress of digital twin channel and intelligent channel, as well as the guidance for the waterborne big data platform construction, this study explores the construction of a waterborne big data platform from the perspective of resilient transportation. In view of the new aim of developing an intelligent and safe national transportation network unveiled by the Guidelines on Developing National Comprehensive Transport Network and the trunk-branch layout of inland water transportation, it is proposed that the resilience of water transport on the one hand is reflected in the role that the water channel system plays in the resilience of the entire transportation network, and on the other hand, it is reflected in the capabilities of safety early warning, prevention and control, emergency response and recovery of the water channel itself. Therefore, the basic functions and core theories of the resilient transportation module for the waterborne big data platform are proposed, and the data acquisition methods are briefly described.

articleTitle: Path planning of underground mining area transportation scene based on improved A* algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The traditional A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> algorithm has the problem of being close to obstacles in path planning. For the narrow transportation scene in the underground mining area, it is evident that the algorithm cannot provide a safe path. This paper proposes an improved A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> algorithm that introduces the cost of obstacles. The cost of obstacles in the scene is considered in the heuristic function, and a safer feasible path is obtained by smoothing. The experimental site is built for actual vehicle experiments. The results show that the improved A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> algorithm with obstacle cost can meet the actual driving needs of intelligent mining vehicles in underground mining transportation scenarios.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis and simulation of LNG leakage and diffusion under different wind speeds
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: This article focuses on the changes in LNG concentration under different wind speed levels and atmospheric stability levels. Emulation program is used to conduct leakage and diffusion simulation analysis, and the range impact brought by LNG under different conditions is obtained. It is concluded that when closer to the leakage source, the higher the wind speed and LNG concentration, the greater the safety hazards; When the distance from the leakage source exceeds a certain distance, the higher the wind speed, the lower the LNG concentration. The atmospheric stability has little impact on the changes in LNG concentration. The more stable the atmosphere, the higher the LNG concentration, and the greater the potential safety hazards. Exploring the impact of ground roughness on LNG gas diffusion, keeping other conditions unchanged, and simulating ground roughness, the simulation shows that the impact of ground roughness is relatively small. This simulation experiment provides certain theoretical support for leak handling and safety prevention in the actual situation of LNG powered ship leakage.

articleTitle: A ship pilot on-duty state recognition model based SlowFast network and attention mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The unsuitable state of ship pilots on duty is a potentially unsafe factor in ship navigation. It has become an important issue of water traffic safety to identify the unsuitable state of pilots, reduce water traffic accidents caused by human factors and improve the safety supervision ability of ship navigation. Aiming at the problems of complex lighting conditions, non-fixed driver trajectory and easy occlusion in ship cockpit scenes, a behavior recognition model based on SlowFast network and EPSA attention mechanism is proposed.

articleTitle: Suitability assessment of wave energy supply in China’s offshore shipping based on GIS and multicriteria evaluation factors
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Based on the natural data of wave height and period in the range of $0 \sim 45^{\circ}\mathrm{N}$ and $100 \sim 135^{\circ}\mathrm{E}$, and considering social factors such as water depth, offshore distance, distance from port, and protected area, we propose a wave energy resource assessment model based on geographic information system (GIS) and multi-criteria evaluation factors. This model aims to assess the suitability of wave energy supply in China’s offshore shipping. The results indicate that there are certain areas that are most suitable for wave energy production.

articleTitle: A Big Data Method For The Evaluation Of Ship Domain In Regional Historical Data
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The shipping industry has long been recognized as a high-risk and high-uncertainty sector, where ship collisions represent particularly grave accidents that can lead to catastrophic consequences. Ship domain, a widely employed navigational approach, establishes a safety zone around the ship to ensure safe passage. Extensive research has been conducted on ship domain, with previous studies predominantly investigating the impact of static and dynamic ship parameters, or the effects of the ship’s surrounding environment on the model. This study proposes a novel ship domain method based on regional historical data, with a primary focus on the influence of risk data on the size of the ship domain in the vessel’s navigation area. In this paper, the AIS data of ship in the Zhoushan waters, China was collected, and the method of detecting possible near miss ship-ship collisions from AIS data is used to find the historical risk point data in the ship’s driving area firstly. Through the historical risk point data, the density of historical ship collision accidents in the region was classified into first, secondary, and tertiary levels. The first level indicated frequent occurrences of ship accidents, thereby highlighting areas of high collision risk. Conversely, the third level represented low-frequency historical ship accidents, signifying a low risk of collision. Finally, the shape and size of the ship domain model were determined based on the hierarchical index of historical ship collision accidents. Simulation experiments confirmed the effectiveness of the proposed method, indicating that it can provide accurate estimations of collision risks in ship encounter scenarios.

articleTitle: Effect of creep on tribological properties of water-lubricated tail bearing materials
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Polymers are widely applied in water-lubricated tail bearings. Polymers tend to creep under constant stress. The creep deformation is often ignored in the design, fabrication and operation. In this study, three commonly used water-lubricated bearing materials, ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene (UHMWPE), Feroform T12, and Compac(Thordon), were used to investigate creep deformation on tribological wear properties. Creep properties were tested on a electronic universal testing machine. The friction and wear properties were tested on a multifuctional tribometer. The results showed that creep will increase the friction coefficient and wear amount of the material. The growth amplitude is in the order of UHMWPE, Feroform T12 and Compac. The increase of friction coefficient of UHMWPE decreases with the increase of rotational speed. And it also decreases with the increase of load. Feroform T12 is opposite to UHMWPE. However, the friction coefficient of Compac decreases with the increase of rotational speed at ION and 25N, and increases at 40N and 55N.

articleTitle: A spatial-temporal analysis on maritime accidents with sample point density clustering
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Global maritime accidents have the characteristics of time-space differentiation. By analyzing the data structure of maritime traffic accidents, a method of time-space differentiation analysis of global maritime accidents based on accident point density clustering is proposed. Through the point density analysis method, combined with the data information of maritime traffic accidents in East Asia, the characteristics of time-space variability are studied. The results show that the density centers in East Asia are near the eastern coast of China and the Malay Archipelago, which shows that the eastern coastal waters of China and the Malacca Strait are always hot spots for accidents in East Asia. The density analysis results of Southeast Asia in different periods show the changing trend of the density of maritime accidents in East Asia. By studying the accident density of different severity, it is found that the density analysis results of very serious accidents and general accidents are almost the same.

articleTitle: Modeling and control study of hydrogen system for port hydrogen equipment
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Most ports are undergoing upgrades targeting “oil to hydrogen” conversion of port equipment, marking the greening of port infrastructure has gradually become a new development direction. The proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC), as a power source using hydrogen as reactant, is clearly an ideal power source for port greening because of its high efficiency, cleanliness and low vibration. The hydrogen system as the core of PEMFC is especially important for the control of the hydrogen system. Based on the joint simulation of AMESim and Simulink, this paper establishes we propose a fuel cell anode pressure control method based on variable-domain fuzzy PI control, and introduce an additional fuzzy controller to obtain the expansion coefficient, so as to adjust the fuzzy domain of the fuzzy PI controller in real time without changing the fuzzy rules of the fuzzy PI controller. The simulation results show that the variable domain fuzzy PI control has smaller overshoot and shorter regulation time compared with fuzzy PI control and PI control, and has better adaptability to sudden changes in load, and it has positive influence on the stable control of anode pressure of fuel cell.

articleTitle: Sensorless PMSM Control Algorithm for Rim-Driven Thruster Based on Second-order Sliding Mode Observer
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of poor speed and position observation performance of the Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) of rim-driven thruster (RDT), a second-order sliding mode observer based on super-twisting algorithm (STA) is presented. The new algorithm to external interference of and effectively weakens the “chattering“ phenomenon. The new algorithm can effectively suppress the sliding mode chattering and retains the advantages of traditional sliding mode observer algorithm such as strong robustness and insensitivity. The simulation results show that the speed and position error and chattering of the proposed second-order sliding mode observer are reduced compared with traditional SMO.

articleTitle: Fluid mixing optimization strategy of catalytic reactor for marine SCR system
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: With the development of green shipping, the demand for control and treatment of ship exhaust emissions is gradually upgraded. The implementation of Tier III of MAPOLE Convention has put forward higher requirements for NOx emission reduction. Selective catalytic reduction (SCR) is one of the most widely used technologies for denitrification of Marine exhaust gas, which has important research significance. In this paper, the influence of the distance between urea nozzle and catalytic converter on the mixing uniformity of exhaust gas and urea water was studied. A catalytic reactor model was established to simulate the uniformity of urea solution at the end of catalytic converter with different distance of urea nozzle. A test bench of SCR system was built (the diesel engine used was 4135Ca type) to verify the simulation results. And combined with the actual engineering application, the optimal distance between urea and catalytic converter was determined as 5D(D is the diameter of the air inlet pipe).

articleTitle: Motion Prediction of Tugboats Using Hidden Markov Model
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The cooperation of tugboats is necessary for the entry and berthing of large boats inside the area of port. Tugboats are effective for assisting in port operations due to their small size and adaptable handling. However, because of the peculiarities of tugboat operation, tugboat motion control has become a popular topic for study. The initial phase in motion control, which can efficiently increase tugboat operation management, is the motion prediction of tugs. Moreover, if the trajectory of tugboats can be precisely predicted, it will be possible to anticipate the existence of unjustified towing operations or poor inter-tug cooperation, making the operating environment in the port’s internal waters safer. The widely-used motion prediction methods, such as long short-term memory techniques and other neural networks, are effective in normal ship manoeuvre. As a widely used prediction method, the hidden Markov model is rarely used in motion prediction. This paper uses the hidden Markov model to learn the behavior pattern of the tugboat in the port from the historical traffic flow. Firstly, for the data generated by simulation, the hidden Markov model is used to first calculate the state transition probability of the tugboat’s rudder angle, heading and speed. Secondly using the state of the previous moment and the calculated state transition probability to predict the state of the tugboat at the future moment. Thirdly, predicting the possible path points of the tugboat in the future according to the predicted tugboat state and predict the motion trajectory of tugboat, and finally analyze the error between the predicted trajectory and the actual simulated trajectory to verify the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Real-time traffic conflict identification using Bayesian Hierarchical Approach at Merging Area in the Environment of Connected and Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The lane-changing maneuvers of vehicles at freeway merging areas can result in a substantial increase in crash risk. The implementation of a connected and autonomous vehicle (CAV) environment is anticipated to decrease the associated conflict risk of such maneuvers, by utilization of surrounding traffic information. To investigate the potential conflict situations that may arise during multi-vehicle interactions by taking advantage of CAV environment, this study proposes a Bayesian hierarchical algorithm to identify traffic conflicts in real-time during mandatory drivers’ merging behavior. The Bayesian hierarchical model consists of observation vehicle conflict layer and prior distribution layer. The MCMC sampling method was utilized to calibrate the model parameters by generating a Markov chain. Two methods including image discrimination and posterior distribution comparison are combined to ensure reliable convergence diagnosis of Markov chain. The results show that the Markov chain for each parameter gradually stabilizes over iterations and the posterior probability density is consistent with the specified prior function and likelihood function. Additionally, the flexibility of this approach significantly enhances the ability to analyze traffic conflict from the real world using applied statistics. The findings of this research have the potential to encourage cautious driving behaviors and provide useful insights for driver safety in the future, especially in the context of CAVs.

articleTitle: A Simulator Study on the Minimum Safety Net Distance between Tunnel and Interchange Exit of Mountainous Expressway
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In the design of some mountainous expressways, the spacing between tunnels and interchanges usually can’t meet the requirements of the design specification because of the limitation of mountainous terrain and the scope of land use. In order to research the minimum safe distance between tunnel and interchange exit under the condition of insufficient length of subgrade, an experimental study was carried out by driving simulator. The virtual simulation scenario of the six-lane mountainous highway with a design speed of 80 km/h was established according to a real road engineering project, and four kind of net distance between the tunnel and the interchange exit were taken as the experimental conditions. Speed and lane crossing points were selected as key evaluation indicators to study the driving risk of drivers on such road section. The results o show that:(1)the net distance between tunnel and interchange exit has a significant impact on the lane crossing position when the driver leaves the main line;(2)under the condition of limited length of subgrade, there is not a good safe driving environment for drivers to drive out of the main line from the inner lane. Finally, based on the driving behavior analysis results, the design recommendation value of the minimum safety net distance between tunnel and interchange exit is proposed, and the corresponding suggestions for traffic organization are also put forward.

articleTitle: Research on full-range autonomous navigation decision making of ships based on finite state machines
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Intelligent ship is a major trend of future ship development, and ship intelligent navigation decision is one of the key technologies of intelligent ship. In order to further improve the level of ship intelligence and informatization and strive to realize the full autonomous navigation of the ship from berth to berth, this paper proposes a full-range autonomous navigation decision-making method of the ship based on finite state machine. Firstly, the full-range autonomous navigation is divided into different navigation scenarios according to the navigation task. Secondly, based on the finite state machine theory, the ship autonomous navigation decision model is constructed. Finally, the experimental verification is carried out in the simulation system based on the constructed autonomous navigation decision model. The experimental results show that the ship can realize the full-range autonomous navigation based on the model proposed in this paper, which verifies the feasibility of the construction method and can effectively support the ship autonomous navigation.

articleTitle: A Study of Speed Control Strategies for Lanes Open to Traffic During the Reconstruction and Expansion of Ten-lane Expressway
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: To ensure traffic safety during road construction, this study investigates speed control strategies for lanes open to traffic in the “six-to-ten” expressway reconstruction and expansion project in Guangdong, China. Firstly, international projects and specifications on speed limits for highway work zones were examined and analyzed to maintain the design speed of the six-lane open-to-traffic construction zone during the highway expansion as a reference. Secondly, real-time speed characteristics of the studied expressways were measured and analyzed during construction.
