Finally, a traffic simulation model using VISSIM was built for the studied expressway during construction, with real-time traffic volume and vehicle proportions loaded to simulate running speeds. The simulation results suggest a recommended speed limit of 80 km/h for the studied expressway. The research methods and results of this study can provide valuable insights into speed control for future projects involving the ’’six to ten’’ highway reconstruction and expansion in China.

Author Keywords: Speed Control Strategy of Lanes Open to Traffic

articleTitle: Research on the Mechanical Properties of TPU Composite Fiber Membrane and Its Inflatable Structural Components
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The reliability of marine evacuation systems is of paramount importance for the personal safety of crew members. This paper aims to improve the reliability of marine evacuation systems by proposing a constitutive model for TPU composite membranes and a deformation prediction model for inflatable beams. The constitutive model for the TPU membrane is based on the continuum theory of mechanics. Its effectiveness is validated through a series of off-axis angle stretching tests, and the model’s predictions fit well with the data, with errors within 10%. This model exhibits high efficiency and accuracy compared to micro-scale models. The deformation prediction of the inflatable members is based on the Le Van inflatable beam model, considering multiple influencing factors. The effectiveness of this model is verified through a comparison with bending and axial loading experiments, demonstrating its ability to better describe the shear effects of inflatable members during the bending process compared to the Le Van model. The research presented in this paper provides a systematic and reliable theoretical model for composite material inflatable members.

articleTitle: Analysis of multi-year variation characteristics of sea ice in Chukchi Sea
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In recent years, the navigational capacity of Northwest Passage in Arctic has been improved due to climate change. The Chukchi Sea, located on the north side of the Bering Strait, is a key area of the Northwest Passage and one of the most representative areas of sea ice variability. The sea ice extent was calculated using sea ice concentration data, and then the temporal and spatial variation characteristics of sea ice extent and thickness in Chukchi Sea were analyzed. The results show that the sea ice has significant seasonal and interannual variabilities. The ice began melt in May, reaching the minimum extent in September, and then began to freeze again. Meanwhile, the sea ice extent decreases year by year. By analyzing the monthly average thickness of the sea ice, it is found that the sea ice grows from October to April of the next year, and the growth rate during the period is gradually decreasing. The study provides valuable information for safe Arctic navigation in the Northwest Passage.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Impact of Replacing Low Sulfur Marine Gas Oil for Ship’s Main Engine on Fuel Injector
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: With the introduction of sulfur limitation orders and emission control area policies, ocean going vessels using high sulfur heavy fuel oil need to replace low sulfur marine gas oil (LSMGO) when entering the restricted area. However, during the replacement of LSMGO, it will have a certain impact on the fuel injector of the ship’s main engine. This article takes a typical engine fuel injector stuck fault event during oil change as an example, and analyzes specific issues from several aspects such as the structure, working principle, oil change operation process and requirements, heavy fuel oil characteristics, LSMGO characteristics, impact of fuel mixing performance, and failure phenomena of the fuel injector. In response to the above practical problems, this article will focus on proposing corresponding countermeasures from the aspects of oil change operation process, temperature and viscosity control, LSMGO lubricity, etc. In practical applications, this method can effectively avoid the occurrence of related faults.

articleTitle: Towards navigational risk identification on a remotely controlled ship with seafarers onboard
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Maritime autonomous surface ships (MASS) have been expected as the future direction in the maritime industry, with four types degrees of autonomy (DoA) defined by the International Maritime Organization. Most studies focus on identifying risk influencing factors (RIFs) on MASS with a high level of DoA, i.e., MASS DoA 3 or 4. However, RIFs identification on MASS DoA 1 or 2 has not been obtained a wide concern by academics. This paper focuses on risk identification analysis of the remotely controlled ship with seafarers onboard (i.e., MASS DoA 2) by incorporating failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA) and risk matrix. Firstly, we identify this kind of intelligent ship’s potential failure modes (FM) concerning the policy documents, existing publications and practical trials. Secondly, we proposed a three-level hierarchical model to identify the potential RIFs. Consequently, each RIF’s occurrence probability and associated effects are evaluated using the probability index (PI) and consequence index (CI) in a given risk matrix. Furthermore, the risk index of these RIFs under diverse FMs is obtained by aggregating the PI and CI. The risk identification analysis can provide critical RIFs for making risk control options for the remotely controlled ship with seafarers onboard by the shipping company, maritime safety administration, and ship designers.

articleTitle: A PID Control Method of Rotative Speed Difference Base on New Shape Hovercraft
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The hovercraft is suspended in the water by the air cushion, which has the advantages of high speed, high capacity, amphibisity performance, etc., but also leads to a high-speed steering difficulty. In order to solve this problem, this paper proposes a new form of hovercraft named “Qiyu”, which designs the hull to be round and arranges the dual drives in a central symmetrical manner on both sides of the hull. In addition, to make the “Qiyu” control more efficient and stable, a PID control method based on the dual drive transfer difference is proposed, which can control the drives for smooth steering. To verify the novel hovercraft, we built a bench platform that allows the “Qiyu” to be fixed above for in-situ steering testing. The results of test showed that the “Qiyu” took 8 seconds for 20° steering and 20 seconds for 40° steering. Compared with the traditional ship type and control methods, the proposed “Qiyu” has obvious advantages in steering function, and its control method has great potential for path tracking research.

articleTitle: Research on human factors of ship grounding accident based on HFACS
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Ship grounding accidents referred to incidents where a vessel accidentally ran aground or became stranded at the seafloor or near the shoreline, resulting in significant human casualties and economic losses. With the growth of maritime trade and the increasing busyness of ship traffic, the risk of ship grounding accidents escalated. Consequently, preventing and controlling such accidents became a critical topic in ship operation management. The Human Factors Analysis and Classification System (HFACS) model, widely applied in aviation, aerospace, rail, shipping, and other fields, served to identify and evaluate the fundamental causes of accidents. By categorizing accident causes into individual, team, organizational, and external environmental factors, the HFACS model shed light on the various factors’ roles in ship grounding accidents, offering guidance and recommendations for accident analysis and prevention. Building upon this, the present study utilized the HFACS model to analyze the human factors of a ship accident, revealing the causal chain: Lack of organizational atmosphere-Supervision violation-Improper management of ship resources-Decision error. Based on these findings, corresponding safety management suggestions were proposed, aiming to provide reference for accident analysis and prevention.

articleTitle: Extension Integrated Control of Electric Vehicles AFS/DYC Based on LQR
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: A hierarchical integrated control strategy of the active front wheel steering system (AFS) and direct yaw moment control (DYC) was developed to compensate for the active front wheel steering system’s lack of vehicle stability control caused by tire lateral force saturation and minimize the power consumption of the executive system. The upper controller divides the vehicle operating state into stable, transitional, and unstable states using the extension phase plane to implement the real-time division of the operating state. The vehicle’s yaw rate and side slip angle are tracked in real time by the lower controller using the linear quadratic optimal adjustment method (LQR). The additional front wheel angle and additional yaw moment are output at the same time that the weight matrix of the optimization objective function is modified depending on the correlation function value. The co-simulation platform was built by Simulink and Carsim, and the two-lane change condition and sinusoidal steering experiments were carried out respectively. The results demonstrate that the integrated control strategy based on extension LQR can successfully compensate for the active front wheel steering system’s shortcomings. The yaw rate, side slip angle, and power consumption of the executive system are reduced.

articleTitle: Overall Layout Optimization of an Unmanned Hovercraft Considering Multiple Aerodynamic Interferences
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In order to weaken the adverse aerodynamic interferences between the hull and the aerodynamic devices like the ducted air propeller, lift fan and bow thruster, and get better aerodynamic performance for an unmanned hovercraft, the aerodynamic performance prediction and flow field characteristics analysis of the hovercraft were carried out first in this paper based on the numerical simulation method. Then, the overall layout optimization work of the hovercraft was conducted considering the multiple interferences between the hull and the aerodynamic devices. The results indicate that by optimizing the distance between the hull and the ducted air propeller, the shape of the engine room, the height and horizontal deflection angle of the bow thruster, the adverse aerodynamic interferences can be weakened obviously, and the effective thrust margin of the whole ship is improved.

articleTitle: Study on the effects of replacing mineral powder with HGM on the cooling performance and road performances of asphalt pavement
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In order to alleviate the rutting and urban heat island effect due to the high temperature of asphalt pavement, this study replaces part of mineral powder with hollow glass microspheres(HGM), and investigates its effects on the road performances of asphalt pavement. In this study, micron-sized hollow glass microspheres with different replacement rates (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) are mixed into AC-13 and SMA-13 mixtures by replacing mineral powder with equal volume, and the optimal replacement volume of HGM, the cooling performance and road performances of the two mixtures are studied by laboratory simulated radiation test, rutting test, freeze-thaw splitting test and Schellenberg binder drainage test, etc. The results show that for AC-13 mixture, with the increase of replacement rate of HGM, the cooling effect is improved up to 5.2°C, the high temperature performance and low temperature crack resistance are improved and moisture damage resistance is decreased. When the replacement rate reaches 100%, the freeze-thaw splitting strength ratio has exceeded the specification requirements. For SMA-13 mixture, with the increase of replacement rate of HGM, the cooling effect is also improved and the highest is 9.0°C, the high temperature performance is improved and the anti-scattering performance is increased, but the moisture damage resistance, low temperature crack resistance and the drainage resistance are decreased. When the replacement rate reaches 100%, the freeze-thaw splitting strength ratio of the mixtures can no longer meet the specification requirements. In addition, the incorporation of HGM reduces the fatigue resistance of AC-13 and SMA-13 mixtures. According to the effects on both of cooling performance and road performance, it is suggested that the best replacement rate of HGM is 40%-60%, at which time AC-13 mixture and SMA-13 mixture can be cooled down about 2.4°C-3.2°C and 3.7°C-6.1°C respectively.

articleTitle: The effect of creep on the lubrication property of rubber-plastic composite water-lubricated bearings
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The deformation of water-lubricated bearings liner has a direct effect on lubrication properties. However, creep deformation is a key factor that has often been neglected in water-lubricated bearing design, manufacture, and operation. This paper investigated the creep deformation of rubber-plastic composites with different thicknesses. The creep effect on lubrication performance was also discussed. Creep tests were conducted using an electronic universal tensile tester. Based on the test results, the creep constitutive equation for rubber-plastic composites was determined. The lubrication model based on the creep constitutive equation was established to evaluate the water film pressure and thickness. The results showed that creep reduces the water film pressure and thickness of the water-lubricated stern bearing, and results in the loading region contraction. The shape contraction position of the water film shape in the outlet area shifts to the central position, and the depth of the contraction depression decreases. By reducing the thickness of the rubber-plastic composite, the water film pressure and thickness are increased. The shape of the water film in the outlet area shrinks and the position gradually shifts away from the center.

articleTitle: Matching path optimization of carpooling mode for private cars considering real-time traffic conditions and passenger satisfaction
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Private carpooling is an effective choice to ensure travel comfort and improve resource utilization. This article aims to improve the quality and efficiency of private carpooling services, in order to alleviate urban traffic congestion and environmental pollution. The paper introduces real-time traffic data from multiple sources and combines passenger satisfaction evaluation indicators (waiting time, maximum riding time, carpooling preferences, etc.) to construct a dynamic path matching optimization model for private carpooling modes. This model achieves goals such as optimal path, high passenger travel satisfaction, and maximum carpooling ratio. The methods used in this study include real-time traffic data collection and processing methods, construction and optimization methods of passenger satisfaction evaluation indicators, the design of a path matching optimization model based on traffic conditions, and a description of the private carpooling mode matching path optimization method considering real-time traffic conditions and passenger satisfaction. The method uses passenger satisfaction as the optimization goal, and combines traffic condition information to match the path, thereby achieving path optimization for private carpooling services. The experimental results show that this method can effectively improve the quality and efficiency of private carpooling services, while reducing travel time and costs. Under the influence of real-time traffic data and passenger satisfaction evaluation indicators, the method can choose a more suitable travel path, improve passengers’ travel experience and satisfaction.

articleTitle: Joint Intensity and Event Framework for Vehicle Detection in Degraded Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Images captured by traditional cameras inevitably suffer from quality degradation under adverse conditions (e.g., low-light, snowy and foggy), this will jeopardize the safety of the self-driving system. Unlike traditional cameras, event cameras can work stably in high dynamic range scenarios, capture accurate motion clues of objects in motion scenes. In this paper, we propose a RGB-Event fusion framework to achieve robust vehicle detection in degraded conditions. Firstly, we design a dual-stream feature extraction network to extract modality-specific features. Secondly, we propose a Feature Align Module (FAM) to align the feature space of the two modalities. Finally, we present a simulated RGB-Event dataset for vehicle detection. It contains variable weather and lighting conditions collected in Panosim. Experimental results on the proposed dataset show that our proposed method can outperform the SOTA framed-based method and RGB-Event method by 2.4%, 7.7% in mAP50 and 4.2%, 8.9% in mAP50:95, respectively.

articleTitle: Visual Navigation Method and Simulation Validation
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In scenarios such as inland rivers, automatic navigation for marine vessels is becoming more and more important. To improve the effect of automatic navigation, a visual navigation method based on machine learning for vessels is designed, and simulation validation is conducted. Firstly, vessel images are captured by using visual sensing technology. A semantic segmentation model is employed to separate the shoreline from the water region and identify the shoreline. Secondly, based on the identified shoreline, a reference anchor point is set for the vessel’s navigation. The vessel’s automatic navigation is achieved through a control algorithm. Finally, the proposed visual navigation method is validated through a simulation platform. Simulation experiments have shown that in simple inland waterway scenarios, the proposed method enables autonomous navigation of the vessel.

articleTitle: Influence Analysis of Podded Propulsors Installation Position Based on Self Propulsion Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The propulsion efficiency of cruise ship is an important indicator to measure the propulsion performance and reliability of cruise ship. This article is based on the self propulsion simulation method of the cruise ship propelled by podded propulsors in still water conditions. By analyzing the layout position of the podded propulsors on the cruise ship, the thrust spacing between the two podded propulsors, and the rotation direction of the propeller, the propulsion efficiency values of the cruise ship under fixed self propulsion points are compared, and optimization of the cruise ship’s propulsion efficiency is achieved. Firstly, the cruise ship self propulsion simulation model is built based on STAR-CCM+ simulation software. Then, a single parameter influence analysis is conducted on the layout position, thrust spacing, and propeller rotation direction of the cruise ship’s podded propulsors at the self propulsion point. Based on the flow field analysis results, the propulsion efficiency is explained and optimized. The research results show that the podded propulsor is in its initial position and the propeller rotates inward, resulting in the highest propulsion efficiency.

articleTitle: Structural Design and Experimental Verification of Wave Adaptive Rescue Boat
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Existing rescue boats are prone to capsize and poor wind and wave resistance in the rescue process. To solve this problem, this paper proposed a catamaran wave adaptive rescue boat based on automobile suspension technology capable of resisting wind and waves under class 4 sea state. Combined with the design requirement of the rescue boat, the buoyancy required by the rescue boat is calculated using 3D modeling software. The drag force experienced by the rescue boat during its voyage is calculated by computational fluid dynamics simulation software and empirical formulas. According to the resistance, the power required for the rescue boat to travel at the designed speed is determined, and the propulsion system of the rescue boat is designed based on it. Further, a sailing test of the rescue boat was completed under different sea conditions, and its sailing stability and wave adaptivity were analyzed. The experimental results show that the stability of the main hull of the rescue boat is much higher than that of the buoyancy tank. Experiment results show that the rescue boat presented in this paper has good wave-damping ability, which lays an excellent technical foundation for safe and efficient human rescue under severe sea conditions.

articleTitle: Design of a test platform for remote control of inland ships and a mixed virtual-real method
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: A design method for an autonomous navigation intelligent test platform that includes collision analysis, water flow simulation, and multi-ship intersection for tortuous, narrow and crowded inland waterways is proposed. The method uses the Fossen ship model as the ship motion prediction method, U3D as the scene view, and PhysX as the collision physics model. To address the problem of a sharp increase in computational load in congested multi-ship inland waterway scenarios, a layered approximate model oriented to analysis requirements is proposed. This significantly reduces computational load while significantly improving visual effects and collision analysis realism. At the same time, the method establishes a trajectory repair method based on a simplified ship motion model and implements a projection method from real discontinuous data to the test platform based on this foundation to achieve virtual-real integration. By simulating delays and constructing congestion, the platform built by this method can provide navigation scenarios that are highly consistent with reality for remote driving research and lay a foundation for related research.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Ship Target Recognition in Multi-Band Infrared Images Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Infrared thermal imaging technology can not only detect ships through obstacles such as smoke, fog, and haze, and realize continuous passive observation day and night, but also observe the external details of ships and subsequently identify and track targets. Therefore, infrared ship target recognition plays a vital role in maritime traffic management and ship navigation safety. Different deep-learning algorithms and infrared images of different bands can easily affect the effect of ship target recognition. This paper selects three representative deep learning algorithms, RetinaNet, Cascade R-CNN and CenterNet, to carry out ship recognition experiments on multi-band infrared ship images. In terms of experimental accuracy, the Cascade R-CNN algorithm demonstrates a high level of recognition accuracy, particularly for small ships. It outperforms other algorithms in terms of recognition accuracy. On the other hand, the RetinaNet algorithm excels in achieving both high precision and fast processing speed. When it comes to experimental speed, the CenterNet algorithm exhibits a faster running speed compared to others. However, CenterNet’s recognition accuracy is slightly lower, especially for small ships. From the perspective of multi-band infrared images, it is observed that long-wavelength Infrared (LWIR) images have a poor recognition effect on small ships. Conversely, short-wavelength infrared (SWIR) images show better recognition performance compared to the LWIR images. By comprehensively considering the accuracy and speed, evaluating the performance of the algorithms in multi-band infrared images, and selecting the best combination to achieve the optimal effect of ship target recognition in practical application, to meet the needs of maritime surveillance.

articleTitle: Analysis of axle load spectrum of highway trucks in Shandong Province
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The axle load spectrum offers a more complete and precise description of traffic load, which is a key influencing factor in asphalt pavement design and management. The Rongwu Highway’s network toll collection system was employed in this study to gather vehicle data for the road stretch surrounding Dongying Toll Station in Shandong Province. In order to analyze the axle load spectrum of six different types of trucks with single-axle and single-tire, single-axle and double-tire, double-axle and triple-axle, we counted the overload vehicles, summarized and grouped the truck type classification, axle type classification, and axle group distribution. According to the conclusions, the trucks of type 3 make up the largest portion of the research area, accounting for half and more. All types of trucks’ single-axle and single-tire axle weight is primarily concentrated in below 100kN, single-axle and double-tire axle weight are likewise the same. The weight of the double-axle is mostly distributed between 18kN and 108kN. The weight of the triple-axle is less than 150kN. All types of trucks’ axle load spectra exhibit blatant double-peak characteristics in this particular axle group. The highway network toll system can be used to its full potential by combining the observed axle load spectrum with traffic control and real-world circumstances. This gives engineers maintenance and future highway service life forecast the support they need.

articleTitle: Study on Improvement of Typical Chemicals Tank Washing Water Treatment Based on Catalytic Technology in the Yangtze River
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The liquid bulk cargo throughput of inland ports in the Yangtze River system reaches 230 million tons, and there are more than 250 types of dangerous chemicals in waterway transportation. The tank washing operation of bulk liquid chemical ships due to cargo exchange and other reasons would produce tank washing water containing liquid bulk cargo residues. In 2017, the tank washing water of the Yangtze River trunk line reached about 1.15 million tons. The process of tank washing water treatment is complex and the cost is high correspondingly. Most of the received tank washing water is sent to the wastewater treatment plant for treatment. The existing treatment processes for wastewater in the ports can effectively degrade chemical oxygen demand, but some characteristic pollution factors such as benzene series have poor biochemical degradation effect and difficult to meet the discharge requirements. In this study, typical chemicals in the Yangtze River waters are selected to carry out experimental research on the treatment effect of photocatalytic technology to chemical tank washing water. The results show that the treatment efficiency of chemical tank washing water can be significantly improved by modifying the traditional photocatalytic materials. Combined with the traditional wastewater treatment process, the discharge of chemical tank washing water can meet the standard.

articleTitle: An improved artificial potential field for vessel collision-avoidance path planning
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Aiming at the drawbacks of traditional artificial potential field method in local path planning for USV (unmanned surface vehicle), an improved artificial potential field method is proposed. Firstly, establish a model for ship collision risk based on the quaternion ship domain. In the gravitational potential field model, Add the gravity of the given route. In the repulsion field model, the influence factors such as relative position and relative velocity are introduced. Four subdivided zones around the own ship are defined to determine the corresponding virtual repulsive potential to ensure International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea (COLREGS)-constrained behaviour for the own ship’s CA actions. The rationality and superiority of the proposed improved artificial potential field method are verified by simulation and comparison experiments Simulations demonstrate that the method is fast, effective, and deterministic for path planning in complex situations with moving target ships, and has been proved to work effectively in a complex navigation environment.

articleTitle: Distributed Situational Awareness for Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships in Mixed Waterborne Transport: An Ontology-based Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The safety of maritime autonomous surface ships (MASS) in mixed waterborne transport system (MWTS) depends on effective situational awareness (SA) distribution among MASS, manned ships, and various stakeholders, such as Vessel Traffic Service (VTS), Remote Control Center (RCC) and Fairway Shipping Agency. This paper focuses on the research question: How can situational awareness be effectively distributed among these entities in mixed waterborne transport? The research objective is to develop a distributed situational awareness framework that unifies SA among these stakeholders, ensuring safe navigation and compatibility with users of different roles. To achieve this objective, the proposed framework incorporates three key concepts: individual SA, authority-based SA, and distributed SA. Individual SA, previously introduced in our study, is responsible for each ship’s SA, while authority-based SA accounts for the SA of human operators supervising the waterborne transport system, such as VTS operators and fairway agency personnel. Distributed SA generates guiding messages for ships based on the situational awareness from both individual SA and authority-based SA, thereby enabling regulation-based and traffic control-based recommendations for waterborne transport (e.g., ship speed and course adjustments). The research methodology employs ontology-based modelling to implement the framework, constructing a domain knowledge network. A case study is conducted as an essential part of the research methodology, presenting how the framework perform the situational awareness from different aspects and inconsistency detection among manned ships, MASS, VTS operators, and so on. Semantic Web Rule Language (SWRL) is utilized to detect inconsistencies and generate guidance messages for ships. Through these cases, we demonstrate how the proposed Ontology-based framework can reconcile inconsistencies between individual and authority-based SA, leading to a safer and more effective waterborne transport.

articleTitle: A Novel Ship Power System Using Zero Carbon Fuel and its Energy Efficiency Management Method
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Under the background of low carbon development of the shipping industry, the application of clean energy hybrid power system would certainly play an important role for the carbon emission reduction of ships. In this paper, a novel power system using zero carbon fuel in the form of “ammonia fuel engine + permanent magnet synchronous reversible motor + battery + super capacitor” is designed. On this basis, the equivalent energy consumption allocation strategy and the fuzzy control rules are proposed to achieve the energy efficiency management of the hybrid system. The proposed power system using zero carbon fuel and the energy efficiency management method can effectively improve the environmental benefit, meanwhile meeting the ship’s power requirement, and can contribute to the development of low carbon shipping.

articleTitle: Optimal control method of heterogeneous vehicle traffic flow under Connected Vehicle environment
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: With the introduction of intelligent connected vehicles (CVs), the mixed traffic of heterogeneous motor vehicles (including human-driven vehicles (HVs) without networking capabilities and intelligent CVs with networking capabilities) may have negative impacts on the transportation system, and the control and guidance of traffic flow for different types of motor vehicles become more complex. Considering the behavioral differences and information acquisition differences among individual vehicles of different types, an optimal control method for heterogeneous motor vehicle traffic flow based on the user equilibrium (UE) model and Bayesian optimization (BO) algorithm is proposed. Firstly, initial traffic volume is assigned to the network based on the UE model, then a Bayesian optimization model is built using the Gaussian process probability surrogate model and acquisition function to optimize the control strategy of CVs for the improvement of heterogeneous traffic flow. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified using the classic Nguyen-Dupuis network, which demonstrates its good solving efficiency and significant optimization effect.

articleTitle: Trajectory Generation for Autonomous Surface Vessels Based on Bézier Curves
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Autonomous surface vessels have attracted significant attention from scholars in the shipping and marine community in recent years. Researchers have focused on methods that consider the dynamics of the vessel to develop effective trajectory generation strategies for these vessels. Efficient trajectory generation is indispensable, but conventional path planning algorithms based on search and sampling are less applicable. To plan trajectories exclusively in the flat output space, we utilize the differential flatness property. In this paper, we use the basic artificial potential field method for front-end trajectory search and present a method for generating feasible trajectories for these vessels using piecewise Bézier curves. By incorporating Bernstein polynomial basis functions and optimizing the cost function with necessary constraints, we convert the problem into a typical convex quadratic programming format. Finally, we evaluate the efficacy of the method by conducting numerical simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Research on online identification method of ship condition based on improved DBN algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The operating condition of the ship is to describe the change of the required power with time during the navigation of the ship. Accurate real-time identification of the characteristics of the current working conditions and timely adjustment of the relevant control parameters of the strategy have a significant positive effect on further improving the efficiency of energy management. This paper proposes an online identification method of ship condition based on improved deep belief network (DBN). In the traditional DBN algorithm, ship load power data is often considered static, but in fact they are dynamic. Therefore, the differential evolution algorithm is introduced to capture the dynamics of data and apply it to DBN. By constructing the condition identification model based on the improved DBN algorithm, the analysis and judgment of the characteristic parameters of the ship ’s current working condition are carried out to determine the real-time working condition type of the ship. This paper uses real ship load data and compares it with methods based on traditional machine learning models. The experimental results show that it is superior to other algorithms in identification accuracy and operation efficiency. Moreover, it can better capture the dynamics of ship load power data and achieve higher identification rate on different data sets. In summary, the method proposed in this paper is an effective and highly stable ship load power condition identification method, which can be used to optimize the ship energy management strategy and improve the ship operation stability and fuel economy.

articleTitle: Night navigation safety assessment of ships based on actual measurement of port light environment
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: As an important transportation hub connecting land and sea, the port has also experienced rapid expansion, with some ports expanding into inland areas. Various lights such as port construction lights, berth ship lighting, and terminal operation lighting form a cluttered background light, causing light pollution, affecting the recognizability of navigation lights, navigational aids and other navigation lights, and affecting the safety of ship navigation at night. In order to prevent accidents in the port waters and evaluate the safety of large ships at night, this article takes the lighting environment of Heng li Petrochemical berth in Chang Xing Island Port area of Dalian Port as an example, and quantitatively analyzes relevant factors through on-site measurement using optical principles, colorimetry, and visual ergonomics, focusing on the impact of navigational light recognizability, ship light recognizability, and crew visual ergonomics. The influence of complex background light in the port on the recognizability of navigation lights mainly changes the brightness contrast, and has little impact on the color contrast of navigation lights. The illumination of the crane on the terminal is strong, which will have a certain impact on the berthing operations of ships at night. When a ship leaves the port at night, the background light around the terminal does not affect the departure operation. Based on this mechanism analysis, regulatory measures to reduce the impact of background light on nighttime navigation safety are proposed from the aspects of background light control, port lighting environment optimization, and navigational light technical transformation.

articleTitle: The application of floating dikes in the inland waterway regulation project
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The conventional method of low beach protection in the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River is to build low water regulation structures, such as beach protection belt, bottom protection belt, beach protection submerged dike, fishbone dam, groin dam, along dam, etc. In the present study, a single box veneer type energy dissipation floating dike is designed. The floating dike is composed of one tank and one energy dissipation plate fixed on the floating body perpendicular to the water flow. The structure of floating dike is simple. The laboratory investigations show that it has good posture and stability in water flows. Taking the north channel of Zhangjiazhou waterway as the experimental area, a case study has been performed to validate the floating dike for waterway regulation project. Through field application and in-situ observation, it is found that the riverbed in the downstream observation area of energy-dissipating floating dike group changed from violent scour reversal to siltation, indicating that the energy-dissipating floating dike proposed in this paper has obvious effect of reducing scour and promoting siltation, and achieves the goal of river shoal protection. The changes of scour and silt of the riverbed in the test core area are basically consistent with the assumption before the project. The energy dissipation mechanism of floating dike thus would be utilized for the long-term improvement of the flow conditions in inland waterways and river shoal protections.

articleTitle: Research on the Safety Production Risk Assessment in the field of Maritime Communication from Navigation Supporting
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: As a very important part, maritime communication filed having an irreplaceable position in terms of navigation supporting. However, due to the increasingly intense technological warfare, the way that how to reduce communication risk, eliminate hidden dangers for protecting maritime communication supporting field safety, had become one of the important subjects from navigation supporting. This paper used the data that came from Tianjin Communication Center of Northern Navigation Service Center, maritime safety Administration, People’s Republic of CHINA, based on risk management process, using fault tree analysis method, brainstorming method and flow charts method etc. defined related marine communication operation risk events; using cconditional hazard assessment method to analyse and evaluate related risk events’ risk level. At the end of this paper, it has been introduced related prevention and improving measures suggestion toward the serious risks during risk treatments process.

articleTitle: Feature Analysis of Icebreaker Escort Operations in Ice-Covered Arctic Waters
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Some Arctic routes have become seasonal navigational routes due to global warming and receding Arctic ice. Affected by the season and ice area environment, sometimes merchant ships must navigate via icebreaker escort to ensure ships’ safe navigation through the ice-covered waters. This study focuses on the processing and analysis of the navigation trajectory of merchant ships escorted by icebreakers in the Arctic waters. A research framework is proposed for feature analysis of icebreaker escort operations in ice-covered Arctic waters based on the combination of satellite automatic identification system (AIS) data, map information technology, and environmental data of the Arctic region. Firstly, the icebreaker’s satellite AIS data clarify the operation waters. Secondly, the satellite AIS data within the operation waters are used to identify the navigation trajectories for the icebreaker and the escorted merchant vessel. Furthermore, the features of the icebreaker escort operations in ice-covered Arctic waters are analyzed by incorporating the AIS data and environmental data. Finally, the satellite AIS data in 2021 will be used as a case study. The proposed method can be used to provide support for decision-making of escort operations in ice-covered waters.

articleTitle: Study on Friction and Sliding Wear Performance of Thordon Material under Dry Friction and Starved-Water Lubrication
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In order to investigate the effect of dry friction and different degrees of starved-water lubrication on tribological performance of Thordon material. Friction and wear test were carried out on Thordon/GCr15 friction pair using the reciprocation module of Rtec multi-function tribometer. Additionally, the effect of different loads, and different reciprocating frequency under starved lubrication condition was studied. The wear surface morphology of Thordon material was observed by laser confocal microscope (LCM), and the friction and wear performance was analyzed. The friction coefficient increases with the increase of severity of starved condition. Under the starved-water lubrication, the friction coefficient increases with the increase of load and decreases with the increase of reciprocating frequency. The wear of Thordon material is the most serious under the dry friction. The wear volume and specific wear rate of Thordon material increase as the severity of starved-water condition increase. Under the starved-water lubrication, the wear volume increases with the increase of load and reciprocating frequency, and the specific wear rates decrease with the increase of load and reciprocating frequency. This indicates that the severity of starved-water, the load and the reciprocating frequency of sliding friction have a great impact on the friction and wear performance of Thordon material.

articleTitle: Calculation of Towing Resistance for Offshore Towing Operation of Drilling Platform Considering Multi-Factor Constraints
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In order to improve the calculation accuracy of the towing resistance of the offshore towing operation of the drilling platform, it provides a reference for the reasonable matching of the tugboats that meet the requirements. Based on the “Guide to Marine Towing” and the theory of fluid mechanics, comprehensively considering the characteristics of the navigation environment of marine towing operations, and introducing various additional resistance factors such as towline resistance, rough sea resistance, and fouling resistance, a drilling well considering multi-factor constraints is proposed. Calculation method of towing resistance for platform offshore towing operation. The method is applied to the calculation of the drag force of the offshore towing operation of “A drilling platform” in Shengli Oilfield, and the results show that the calculation results of the method proposed in this paper are closer to the actual situation compared with the calculation results of the guide. In order to be scientific and reasonable, the accuracy of the calculation method in this paper is verified.

articleTitle: Estimation of Ship Pollutant Production Based on Ship Dynamic Data and Countermeasures for Ship Pollution Prevention in Inland Water
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In recent years, China’s inland waterway transportation has developed rapidly. During the ship operation and navigation, pollutants such as oily waste, sewage and garbage will be produced, which will have a serious impact to the environment. Since the characteristics of regionality and fluidity of ship pollutions, the Yangtze River trunk line was selected as the research objective. Using the basic calculation method and the calculation method based on AIS ship information, water pollutant loads of ships in the Yangtze River trunk line were calculated respectively. The result is compared with the empirical value form literature data and the characteristics of ship pollutants are analyzed also. Based on the characteristics of ship pollutant load, the feasibility of its reduction in the inland water area is studied.

articleTitle: Multi-dimensional wind energy utilization potential assessment method for port
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Since the existing evaluation methods of wind energy utilization cannot effectively cover the environmental factors in port and the evaluation dimension is too unitary. The article proposes a multi-dimensional wind energy utilization potential assessment method for port, which is based on the port’s wind energy resource characteristics. Considering the unique characteristics of port environments, this article has constructed evaluation models from three dimensions: port wind power potential, life-cycle economics of port wind farm, and life-cycle carbon emissions of wind farm. The article also evaluates and verifies the potential of wind energy utilization in a certain port area of Ningbo-Zhoushan Port, which hopefully can be used as a reference for the assessment of wind energy resource in other ports.

articleTitle: Study on the properties of m-phenylene type unsaturated polyester resin modified asphalt mixtures
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: To improve the low-temperature crack resistance, water stability and fatigue resistance of bridge deck pavements and to reduce the cost, an unsaturated polyester resin (UP) modified asphalt mixture is developed in this paper. The property of the UP modified asphalt mixture is tested by splitting, rutting, low temperature bending, water immersion, freeze-thaw splitting and low temperature bending tests, and is compared with those of matrix asphalt mixture, SBS modified asphalt mixture and epoxy asphalt mixture. The results show that the UP modified asphalt mixture exhibits superior strength, high temperature stability and low temperature cracking resistance in comparison to the SBS modified asphalt mixture. Additionally, its moisture damage resistance and fatigue resistance are similar to those of the SBS modified asphalt mixture. Compared to epoxy asphalt mixture, while there may be some differences in terms of strength, high temperature stability and fatigue resistance, it boasts superior low-temperature cracking resistance and moisture damage resistance.

articleTitle: Adaptive Coordinated Path Following Control of USVs for Offshore Oil Spill Surveillance*
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Offshore Oil spill pollution is a serious threat to marine environments, an adaptive coordinated path following control problem for offshore oil spill surveillance of unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) is studied in this paper. Firstly, the kinematic model of USVs is established by using a fixed coordinate system and a body coordinate system, and the path following error model of USVs is built in the basic coordinate system; Secondly, an variable look-ahead distance is introduced into the traditional line of sight (LOS) guidance law, and an adaptive line of sight (ALOS) guidance law is constructed, such that an adaptive coordinated path following controller is proposed to achieve the task of offshore oil spill surveillance effectively; Finally, the stability of the proposed control system is proved by Lyapunov stability theory. Simulation results are provided to substantiate the effectiveness of the proposed adaptive coordinated path following controller of USVs for offshore oil spill surveillance.

articleTitle: Research on automatic parking assistant system based on path planning
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Parking assistant system can not only replace the driver to park, but also help to reduce the occurrence of accidents during parking. The path planning and control under the typical parallel parking scene cited in the national standard GBT 41630-2022 have been studied. Through the analysis of vehicle motion parameters and the design of the path planning method, the safety and accuracy during the parking process have been validated. Meanwhile, the control strategy can be optimized according to the real-time target trajectory, which is utilized to reduce the parking position deviation and angle deviation. The simulation results show the path planning method can meet the requirement of parking, and the parking process performers excellent.

articleTitle: A Study on Control Switching Mechanism based on Autonomous Ship Guidelines
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In the future, maritime autonomous surface ship(MASS)will be extensively used in maritime cargo transportation. In the process of MASS development, a gradual process of “constrained autonomy to full autonomy” is necessary, so the control system of "man-machine co-driving" is a stage that the MASS must go through. The switching of control rights among autonomous system, shore-based operator and crew on board has also become necessary. At present, there are no standards for the switching mechanism of MASS control right. In order to establish a preliminary MASS control switching mechanism and provide reference for the safety of "man-machine co-driving", this paper makes an analysis and research on the autonomous ship guidelines. The study found that on the basis of the existing autonomous ship specifications, the autonomous ship control switching mechanism can be obtained from the four dimensions of scenario, agent, priority and process. The research results are meaningful to provide reference for the establishment of autonomous ship control switching mechanism and subsequent research.

articleTitle: Investigating the causes of vessel besetting in the ice channel in the Baltic Sea using AIS data and Sentinel imagery
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Icebreaking assistance in ice-covered waters involves the use of icebreaker(s) to create an ice channel for the assisted vessel(s), which facilitate the vessel(s) navigation in ice conditions. However, assisted vessels that follow the icebreaker may become beset in the ice channel. In April 2021, vessel A navigated in the Baltic Sea with the assistance of icebreakers B and C, during which vessel A experienced three instances of besetting within the ice channel. This research endeavors to examine the underlying causes of vessel besetting within the ice channel by analyzing automatic identification system (AIS) data and ice condition data. The preliminary findings indicate that the primary factors that contributed to that besetting were the severe ice conditions and considerable distances between the icebreaker and the vessel. Evidence to suggest that the channel radius influenced the besetting have not been found, but it is hypothesized that the curvature of the ice channel may have impacted the maneuvering capabilities of icebreaker C in the third beset instance.

articleTitle: Principal component analysis of multi-sensor monitoring for LNG leakage
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In order to ensure the suitability of sensors for LNG logistics parks, this article necessitates a comprehensive inspection of LNG storage tanks. This encompasses a thorough analysis of the liquefied natural gas generation mechanism within the park, the arrangement of LNG storage tanks, the distinctive environmental characteristics of the logistics park, and the fundamental principles underlying LNG diffusion. By utilizing detection data from various sensors and conducting principal component analysis, the article ultimately determines the essential sensor types and monitoring parameters applicable to the system.

articleTitle: Trigger event(s) identification for switching operational mode of Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS) are expected to operate in various operational modes (OMs). To support the decision-making on OM switching, navigational risk in three OMs, i.e., manual control (MC), remote control (RC), and autonomous control (AC) had been discussed in our previous studies, while the time for switching is still an open question. Based on our previous studies, this paper proposed a 4-step framework, including the development of Accident Scenario (AS), operational risk comparison, the establishment of Sub-AS, and trigger event(s) determination. In the case study, the scenario is derived from a ship-bank allision accidents, where the 3rd DoA MASS is employed; the inputs of failure modes (FMs) are evaluated in three OMs by interviewees; the results reveal that the MC is the optimal OM to switch to, and when deviation in course occurred, such switching should be performed. Additionally, we found increasing the number of interviewees could reduce the uncertainty and enhance the reliability of results.

articleTitle: Analysing the Mental Workload of Ship Navigators during Emergencies Based on Physiological Detection Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: This paper aims to investigate the characteristics of psychological stress of ship navigators during emergency at sea using physiological detection methods. By collecting the electrocardiogram and skin conductance signals of ship navigators, the changes in psychological stress under different task durations and types were analyzed. The experimental results showed that the psychological stress of ship navigators significantly increased during unexpected events at sea, and both electrocardiogram and skin conductance signals could reflect this change. Compared with electrocardiogram signals, skin conductance signals were more sensitive and accurate, and could more quickly reflect changes in psychological stress. However, in long-term tasks, electrocardiogram signals performed more stably. The results of this study are of great significance for improving the operational safety of ship navigators at sea and thus reducing the occurrence of accidents.

articleTitle: Predicting Drivers’ Speeding Behaviour: A Case-based Reasoning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: To ensure successful road safety controls, several studies have attempted to propose models and theories that explain and predict drivers’ risky behaviour. However, existing research has several limitations including knowledge elicitation, bias, assumption, and interpretation issues. To help identify potential risky driving behaviours and avoid crashes, we have developed a case-based reasoning system that identifies speeding -one of the most common traffic violations. Our proposed system generates the expected value of a targeted traffic situation based on several similar previous cases. We consider four categories of factors, which include demographic information of the driver, vehicle information, road situation, and environmental factors. We examined four scenarios based on traffic crash data in China, and our case-based prediction system demonstrated its merits compared to the widely employed logistic regression model. Our findings will shed light on safety promotion strategies to decrease the rate of speeding and other traffic violations.

articleTitle: MISO Magnetic Induction Communication Transmission Method Based on Pre-coding Within Transmitting Coil Array
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The mutual inductance impedance within the multiple-input single-output (MISO) magnetic induction coil array is the main factor limiting the transmission rate. In this regard, this paper proposes a MISO magnetic communication transmission method based on precoding in the transmitting coil array. Firstly, the source of interference in the coil array of the MISO magnetic induction communication transmitter is analyzed. The impedance matrix of the transmitting coil is estimated according to the frequency of the modulation signal and the physical relationship of the coil. The zero-forcing precoding matrix operation method is used to zero the mutual inductance impedance between different transmitting coils in the impedance matrix, in order to eliminate interference in the transmitting coil array. Secondly, the modulation signal is loaded into each transmitting coil of MISO magnetic induction communication, and the induced electromotive force is generated in the receiving coil through the magnetic induction medium to complete the signal transmission. This method can eliminate the mutual inductance impedance in the transmitting coil array and suppress the interference between coils. In this paper, we design relevant simulation experiments to verify the effect of the proposed method on the information transmission rate of a magnetic communication system. The experimental results show that when the transmission power is greater than 2.5 mW, the data transmission rate is greatly improved compared with the method without zero forcing precoding. When the transmission power reaches 5 mW, the data transmission rate can be increased by about 11%.

articleTitle: Research on the Causal Chain of Marine Engine Accidents Based on HFACS
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Human factors are the leading cause of accidents in ship maintenance management, and there are correlations between human-caused accident causal factors, which are likely to lead to the occurrence of related factors once they occur, thus further expanding the accident losses. In order to further analyze the process and causal mechanism of human-caused accidents in ship maintenance management, the causal factors involved in human-caused accidents are studied and the correlations between them are identified. According to the analysis of literature and accident investigation reports, the human factors of ship accidents in engine have been identified and the original HFACS model has been refined which is suitable for ship engine management. Then, the Apriori algorithm was applied to mine the association rules of the causal factors on 52 human related accident investigation reports, and to reveal the causal chains from the explicit to the implicit layers. The results show that the main cause of accidents in ship engine is not the explicit human unsafe behaviour, but the hidden factors. Inadequate human resources management and improper equipment management at the organization influence level, on the one hand, directly lead to unsafe human behaviour that leading to more accidents, and on the other hand, may indirectly impact on operational planning, maintenance and repair of equipment, and human adaptability, which will increase the incidence of accidents in ships. Good organizational management as well as strict supervision are therefore key factors in preventing human-caused accidents.

Author Keywords: Analysis of causes of human-caused accidents
Human Factors Analysis and Classification System

articleTitle: Optimal Pricing Strategy of Sharing Parking Platform Considering the Perceived Heterogeneity of Inconvenience Costs
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Shared parking has been regarded as an effective means to solve the urban parking problem, but its development is slow due to unreasonable pricing and the inconvenience perceived by parking space owners and travelers in parking sharing. In response to this problem, considering the heterogeneity of perceived inconvenience cost, the optimal pricing strategy of sharing parking platform with two alternative objectives: profit maximization or social welfare maximization are examined by analyzing the decision-making behaviors of the owners and travelers in the two-sided market. And the number of shared participants under the optimal pricing is discussed. Finally, the influence of related factors on the optimal pricing and the number of participants is further explored by numerical examples. The results show that compared with the profit-maximizing platform, social-welfare-maximizing platform’s optimal commission rate and shared parking fee are lower, while the number of shared parking participants is larger when the management cost of successfully matched parking spaces is small. The local authority may set price upper bounds or entry standards for profit-maximizing platform, or provide profit subsidies to encourage the platform to set lower prices, which are helpful to achieve social welfare maximization. When the management cost is too high, neither platform can make profits, and there are no owners and travelers willing to participate in sharing. Improving the convenience of parking sharing, reducing the management cost of shared parking spaces and increasing the curbside parking fee all contribute to motivating the owners and travelers to participate in and promoting the development of shared parking.

articleTitle: A Study on Countermeasures for Railway Traffic Safety Accidents
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The background of increased railroad traffic after the epidemic Safety in operation is the most important issue in railroad operation management, and all railroad companies have made “safety first” as their guideline. In this paper, a further study is conducted on the countermeasures after railroad traffic safety accidents by analyzing the causes and influencing factors of railroad traffic safety accident.

articleTitle: Semantic-driven behavior modeling and recognition of tugboat
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In order to enhance the efficiency of port operations, ensure port safety and improve port water traffic supervision, a semantic model of tugboat behavior in port waters is proposed. This model includes a tugboat navigation behavior semantic recognition model and a tugboat assistance behavior semantic recognition model. The semantic model of tugboat behavior is established by analyzing the behavior characteristics of port tugboats in terms of time, space, semantics, motion characteristics, and association characteristics. This includes constructing an object model, constructing a tugboat behavior relationship model, and modeling tugboat behavior semantics. Based on the established semantic model of tugboat behavior, corresponding recognition algorithms are designed. The recognition algorithm designed based on the semantic model of tugboats is verified by using Shenzhen Yantian Port as the experimental water. The results show that the semantic model of tug behavior in the port area can effectively identify tug navigation behavior and tug assistance behavior, which greatly improves port operation efficiency and supervision efficiency. Overall, the proposed semantic model of tugboat behavior in port waters is a significant step towards improving port safety and efficiency. It provides a comprehensive and reliable method of analyzing tugboat behavior, which can help identify potential problems early and implement solutions promptly.

articleTitle: Ship Lock Scheduling Method of Three Gorges Based on Improved Ant Colony and Surplus Rectangle Fill Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In order to improve the navigation capacity of ship lock of Three Gorges and relieve the backlog of ships, an optimal algorithm for ship lock scheduling is proposed, which integrates improved ant colony algorithm and surplus rectangle fill algorithm. First, the average waiting time of ships and the average utilization rate of lock chamber area is treated as the objective function, the mathematical model of ship lock scheduling problem is constructed. Second, considering the navigation rules of the Three Gorges Dam and the attributes of ships, the concept of ship weight is introduced to determine the ship entry sequence. The global search ability of the algorithm is improved by the pheromone update strategy for the optimal lock chamber arrangement and the path transfer strategy combining adaptive selection and dynamic adjustment. For each iteration the lock chamber arrangement is implemented by the surplus rectangle fill algorithm in order to improve the local search ability. Finally, the actual data of ship lock in the Three Gorges dam is used to verify the performance of the proposed algorithm, and compared with the manual arrangement strategy and CPLEX solution results. The waiting time of the proposed algorithm is reduced by 10.26 % and 2.62%, and utilization rate of ship lock is increased by 8.42 % and 7.31%, respectively. The results show that the proposed algorithm has good performance for ship lock scheduling.

Author Keywords: utilization rate of lock chamber area

articleTitle: A novel vessel route optimization algorithm based on segmented A-star algorithm in inland waterways
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: For inland water transportation, the route planning is closely relevant to the safety and efficiency of vessel navigation. To meet the requirements route planning with variable depths, water flows, navigation rules and other factors for inland ongoing vessels, this paper proposes a segmented A-star (A*) algorithm to optimize inland vessel routes. This algorithm divides the entire navigation waterway to several segments, to avoid the large amount of calculation with excessive grids. For each segment, the optimal route in terms of efficiency and safety is generated by an improved A* algorithm considering navigation rules, water flow, water depth, bridge piers, and vessel maneuverability. The experiments with real hydrologic and terrain data of Wuhan waterway of Yangtze River, show that the proposed method can generate safer and more economical routes in comparison of other algorithms.

articleTitle: Quantitative Analysis of Collision Avoidance Actions Timing for Stand-on Vessels
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The collision avoidance responsibilities of both vessels in two-vessel encounters are defined in COLREGs. When the give-way vessel and the stand-on vessel are identified, it may happen that the give-way ship does not effectively take substantial actions in time for some reason. This way, if a collision happens, the stand-on vessel is still responsible for not taking any actions according to the rules. Since there are only descriptive requirements for the actions of stand-on vessels, it is difficult for officers to accurately understand the reasonable collision avoidance actions timing. From the perspective of ship navigation safety, this paper analyzes the action timing for stand-on vessels, combining the phases of collision accident development. By defining the ship domain at different phases and the possible actions, the earliest and latest timing for standon vessels to take action are both quantified. Finally, based on the simulation results in crossing situations, the factors affecting the timing are analyzed, and the corresponding suggestions are proposed. The research results provide a theoretical basis to further study the behavior of stand-on vessels in the context of intelligent collision avoidance, and practical references of the collision avoidance actions for stand-on vessels.

articleTitle: Navigation Risk Assessment of LNG Carrier in the Shanghai section of the Yangtze River
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: To ensure the navigation safety of LNG Carrier in the Shanghai section of the Yangtze River, the main risk factors affecting navigation were analyzed from the particularity of LNG Carrier and personnel, equipment, management, and environment. The system dynamics method was used to establish the navigation risk management model of the LNG Carrier in the Shanghai section of the Yangtze River, and the interaction relationship between various factors in the system was simulated with the help of Vensim software, and effective management strategies were proposed for the key factors in each subsystem of the system. Based on the results, fog, wind conditions, tides and currents, traffic volume, accompanying tugboats, pilot behavior, VTS monitoring, safety investment, and certification rate are key risk factors for LNG Carrier in the Shanghai section of the Yangtze River. Strategies such as safeguard measures, strengthening VTS monitoring, paying attention to bad weather, reasonably arranging accompanying tugboats, formulating emergency plans for LNG Carrier, and improving pilot boarding and disembarkation procedures can effectively reduce the risk of LNG carrier navigation in the Shanghai section of the Yangtze River.

articleTitle: Systematic analysis of human factors in maritime transportation
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: 65.8% of marine casualties and incidents are attributed to human actions, according to European Maritime Safety Agency. It is even more worrisome given the emerging Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS) in which human factors play an increasingly important role (e.g. remote controlled vessels). Therefore, it triggers a new research question on how to effectively address human factors in the next generation of maritime transport given more complicated traffic and increased automation. One of realistic solutions is to develop a systematic and holistic methodology, capable of conducting human factor analysis under various circumstances depending on crucial influencing factors such as the nature of human behaviors (physical or psychological) and features of the available data (uncertainty level). This study pioneers this development with a new framework for the quantitative analysis of human factors in maritime transport. It first explores the common risk factors, data collection resources, and quantitative analysis methodologies in the literature. With regard to different research objectives, bespoke approaches aiming at specific purposes, i.e., risk-based accident analysis, neurophysiological analysis during navigation, and human reliability performance evaluation for a particular task, are integrated to develop the systematic analysis framework holistically. Compared to piecemeal classical methods, the results show the feasibility and beauty of systematically utilizing assembled methods in different situations and how the new methodology can better fit the increasing demand for human reliability in the maritime transport era involving MASS. The proposed framework can provide a transparent tool to quantify and evaluate human factors for a specific purpose, particularly a hybrid of both physical and psychological concerns. It also generates insights into the whole development process of MASS, from its low to high degrees of autonomation.

articleTitle: Impact Factors and Safety Analysis of Takeover Behavior in Remote Control of Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: With the development and application of artificial intelligence, advanced control theory, mobile communication, and IoT technologies, the Maritime Autonomous Surface Ship (MASS) has gradually entered the development characteristics period of remote control (Level 2). Based on the review of development dynamics and application cases of the remote-controlled ship in recent years, it analyzes the impact factors of operator takeover behaviors from three aspects: network communication, system control performance, and traffic scenarios, it proposed a new development direction of the remote-controlled ship, which could provide theoretical support for scholars in related fields.

articleTitle: An Automated SAR-based Method for Ship Detection in Maritime Surveillance System
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) is an active Earth observation system that can obtain high-resolution ocean images all day and all weather. It can be used for monitoring the marine environment, maritime traffic, and oil spills at sea. SAR provides accurate and real-time ocean information, which can ensure water traffic safety and ecological environment. Therefore, it plays an irreplaceable role in maritime surveillance. At present, deep-learning based object detection methods have achieved certain results in the application of ship detection in SAR images. Ship targets in SAR images have strong angular reflection characteristics, causing some parts of them to have large grayscale values, appearing as scattering points. At the same time, the heading of ship usually has a certain angle with the horizontal direction. Traditional deep-learning models do not have sufficient generalization ability for these situations. Horizontal bounding boxes also contain a large amount of background features, which affects the accuracy of the model. In response to these characteristics, first use convolutional neural network to extract ship features; Secondly, generate oriented proposals to reduce the impact of background features; Thirdly, using Canny and Harris to obtain features of ship edges and scattering points as attention mechanisms to enhance bounding box regression and classification; Finally, optimize the loss function, which will consider the influence of angle. Comparative experiments were conducted on the SSDD dataset, and the experimental results showed that compared to existing methods, the improved model has better ship detection performance and can achieve accurate detection of small ship targets in complex scene SAR images.

articleTitle: Regional Traffic Flow Prediction Model Based on Mobile Signaling Data- A Case Study of Chongqing City
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: With the rapid development of the Internet and the Internet of Things, we can obtain the real-time and massive transportation data. The transportation data can be used to predict the traffic flow trend to reduce traffic congestion, both from the perspective of road users and policy makers. Combined the real-time and massive transportation data with the real-time and massive mobile phone signaling data, the traffic flow trend can be more accurate and practical. The dataset used in this paper consists of two days mobile signaling data from all regions in Chongqing, which was utilized to generate and evaluate the models. In this study, a neural network model is proposed to predict spatio-temporal traffic flow based on mobile phone signaling data in Chongqing, and the model is evaluated by both predicted data and observational data.
