With ActSTT, the proposed method achieves accuracy close to 98% and 99% on public datasets as well as our real cyber-ship dataset SCS, respectively, outperforming the current state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Research on Collision Avoidance Decision-making of Multiple Intelligent Ships Based on Route Exchange
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Vessel collision or near-collision situation is the primary issue in intelligent navigation. Officer on watch (OOW) faces collision avoidance decision-making based on situational awareness and intention recognition. However, in a multi-ship encounter situation, confusion of situational awareness and unclear intentions would make the decision much more complex. Only by collaborating and jointly planning collision avoidance strategies can the collision risk be effectively reduced. In order to make the ship intelligent collision avoidance strategy collaborative, safe and practical, a ship collaborative collision avoidance decision method based on route exchange is proposed. Firstly, the method of identifying ship encounter situations that design a collision risk assessment mechanism is studied and the tactical route exchange model is constructed. Secondly, the ship route exchange is carried out, in which the PSO algorithm is used to plan the trajectories of the conflicting ships in accordance with the collision avoidance rules. Subsequently, Determining and navigating along the accepted route through route exchange and negotiation. Finally, simulation experiment is carried out for the multi-ship encounter situation. The results show that on the basis of route exchange, the planning trajectories are more accurate and meet the practical requirements, which provides a new solution for improving the intelligent navigation and ensuring navigation safety.

articleTitle: A Technical Design of Inland Intelligent 64 TEU Container Ship for Beijing-Hangzhou Canal
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: With the rise and breakthrough of big data, cloud computing, artificial intelligence and other technologies, the shipping industry is transitioning from the era of automation and information to the era of intelligence. Intelligent shipping is a new modern shipping business form formed by the deep integration of modern information, artificial intelligence and other high-tech and shipping elements. In this paper, firstly the stat of art for inland intelligent container ship is introduced, the overview of the inland intelligent 64 TEU container ship is presented. Secondly, the design of 64 TEU container ship is applied in the consideration of optimization. For the integrated design scheme of the ship, the power system, propulsion device, power system layout, power distribution system, power system monitoring, engine room layout optimization, energy conversion, ship-engine and oar matching and propulsion efficiency are integrated into the overall design. Finally, by systematically studying such problems as rapid construction and real-time service of holographic navigation scene map in inland water network area, design and development of shipboard and shore-based information infrastructure of ship-shore collaboration, intelligent cross-domain computing of ship-shore collaboration, etc., the enhanced navigation and navigation support technology of inland intelligent container ship are performed. In the conclusion, the guidance of the design for intelligent 64 TEU container ship is proposed.

articleTitle: A data-driven risk analysis of Arctic ship navigation accidents
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The challenges faced by Arctic navigation, such as uncertain ice conditions, rapid weather changes, limited communication capabilities, and weak navigational safety support, expose it to higher risks. According to the Arctic Council’s statistical report on polar maritime accidents, there were a staggering 2,638 maritime accidents recorded in the Arctic waters between 2005 and 2017, with a fluctuating upward trend. This study aims to collect and analyze ship accident data in the Arctic waters to identify accident scenarios and primary risk factors influencing the safety of Arctic navigation. Drawing upon the accident scenarios in Arctic navigation, the study retraces the primary risk factor states at the time of relevant accidents based on geographical location information. By utilizing data-driven algorithms, a model for ship navigation accident prediction in the Arctic waters was constructed to gain in-depth understanding of the navigational conditions prone to accidents. The research findings hold practical value in improving quantitative risk assessment, with a focus on navigational risks in the Arctic region. The outcomes of this study can assist maritime authorities and shipping companies in conducting risk analysis and accident prevention measures for ship navigation in the Arctic waters.

articleTitle: Detection of abnormal sound in industrial equipment based on classification and outlier calculation
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that there are many abnormal sound types in industrial equipment and few fault samples can be obtained, a method for detecting abnormal sound of industrial equipment is proposed. Firstly, we focus on two improved neural network models: MobileNetV2 based on classification method and Dense AutoEncoder based on outlier calculation method. Combined with the characteristics of neural network, we propose an improved MFCC feature extraction method. In order to improve the training accuracy, the comprehensive perturbation of the training samples is increased by the data augmentation; finally, the influence of hyperparameters on the training effect is analyzed. Experiments shows that the improved method proposed in this paper achieves an excellent recognition rate.

articleTitle: COLREGs-compliant autonomous collision avoidance method based on deep reinforcement learning for USVs
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Collisions between ships seriously threaten the safety of maritime traffic. Meanwhile, more than 80% of maritime accidents are related to human factors. To realize the autonomous collision avoidance of Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs), in this paper, we propose an autonomous collision avoidance method based on Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). Firstly, in order to enable the ship to take collision avoidance actions at the appropriate time and reach the target point as soon as possible, two navigation states are determined based on Quaternion Ship Domain (QSD), that is, the goal-oriented state and the collision avoidance state. Then, we design different state spaces for dynamic and static obstacles to reduce the input of redundant information and speed up the convergence of the algorithm. In addition, COLREGs and navigation practices are taken into account when designing the reward function, so that the agent’s operation is consistent with good seamanship. Finally, on the basis of the Deep Q Network (DQN), the most representative algorithm in DRL, we design experiments of static obstacle scenarios and a variety of dynamic encounter scenarios to test the rationality and effectiveness of the algorithm. The experimental results show that the USV can reach the target point without collision by using the algorithm proposed in this paper, and the decision made by the USV conforms to COLEREGs and navigation experience. This indicates that the proposed algorithm can provide support for ship autonomous collision avoidance decision-making.

articleTitle: Bayesian-based assessment of emergency supply chain resilience and security levels
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The frequency and intensity of natural and manmade disasters are increasing yearly. Explore the resilience and safety level of the emergency supply chain, and this paper analyzes the existing problems of resilience and security of the emergency supply chain from four aspects: coordination and trust among relevant parties, network threat, outsourcing security risk, and uncertainty. Bayesian networks (BN) are proposed to solve these problems based on four main factors: technical, organizational, human, and environmental factors are used to assess the resilience of the supply chain. Through the Bayesian network model and Leaky Noisy-or model, it is found that the information management platform in technical factors and the collaboration in organizational factors have the greatest impact on emergency supply chain disruption, which is 0.6 and 0.57, respectively.

articleTitle: Determination of Channel Boundary and Customary Anchorage Based on AIS Data
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The rapid increase of treatment in seaports is continually posing higher challenges for channel management and construction. Due to the diversity of ship navigation habits, in real-world channels, there are traffic management problems caused by ambiguous channel boundaries and the existence of unofficial customary anchorages, which impend scientific planning and full utilization of water areas. In this research, we propose a method based on Automatic Identification System (AIS) data to explicitly determine channel boundaries and customary anchorages, this is achieved by parallel processing of large-scale AIS data, vessel’s navigation characteristics analysis based on probability theory, rasterization processing of spatial data, etc. It aims to quantify and visualize the characteristics of the complex channel traffic network, thereby assisting the management and planning of the channel network as well as optimizing the management of the coastal channel traffic network. Extensive numerical studies utilizing AIS data from Hangzhou Bay are illustrated to evaluate the proposed method. The results demonstrate that the proposed method is effective in determining the channel boundary and customary anchorage. Moreover, the method provides some ideas for the digitalization and intelligence of the coastal channel network analysis.

articleTitle: Identification of pilots’ mental workload under different flight phases based on a portable EEG device
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Excessive mental workload situations in pilots will increase their reaction time or cause them to react inappropriately which could impair flight safety. This paper attempts to identify the mental workload of pilots under various flight phases according to a single-flight task in a realistic flight simulator and guides pilots to reasonably allocate their attention to improving flight safety. The scores of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration-Task Load Index (NASA-TLX) scales of each pilot under different flight phases were analyzed by a extensive statistical analysis. The results show that the mental workload levels from high to low are as follows: landing, takeoff, and cruise. Meanwhile, power spectral densities (PSD) of different bands were extracted as features based on a portable 5-channel EEG device, and the Kruskal-Wallis test was used to select features with great significance. And the performances of three machine learning algorithms, the K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), random forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM), were compared. The RF model was shown to perform the best in terms of robustness and classification accuracy. This research also proves that it is feasible to research pilots’ mental workload using this portable 5-channel EEG device. The findings of this research could contribute to researches under real flight conditions.

articleTitle: Computer Vision-Based Pointer-Style Mechanical Dial Reading Method for LNG Terminal Safety
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: As the demand for liquefied natural gas (LNG) continues to grow, the number of LNG terminals is increasing. To ensure safe operation at LNG terminals, various types of metering instruments with pointer-style dials are installed to monitor the real-time operating status of the LNG facilities. aiming at the problems of low accuracy, low real-time detection efficiency and high risk of traditional manual reading methods, a deep learning pointer instrument automatic reading method based on PP-PicoDet and BiSeNetV2 is constructed. Firstly, the PP-PicoDet object detection algorithm is used to locate the position of the instrument dial in the complex background image. Then, the BiSeNetV2 semantic segmentation algorithm is used to segment the pointer and scale areas from the background image, to fit a circular dial using the least-squares-circle function and fit the pointer as a straight line using the curve-fit function, Finally, the angle method algorithm developed independently is used to calculate the instrument reading. The algorithm is experimentally verified by selecting the liquid level meter and pressure gauge. The results show that the reading error is about 2%, and the average recognition time is about 415ms, which has good accuracy and speed, and meets the actual requirements of instrument reading recognition, realizing the intelligent real-time safety monitoring of LNG terminals.

articleTitle: A CNN-based Method for Multisensor and Multiscale Fault Diagnosis of Marine Electric Thruster Bearings under Noise Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Bearings are indispensable supporting parts of the marine electric thruster (MET). Due to long-term work in harsh marine environments, bearings are more prone to failures. However, the diagnosis of MET bearings using vibration signals is a difficult task since the collected signal is nonlinear and nonstationary, and its fault features are easily swallowed by environmental noise. This paper proposes a novel multisensor and multiscale convolutional neural networks (MM-CNN) method to extract different scale features under low signal-to-noise ratios and diagnose the faults of MET bearings. Firstly, the principal component analysis is introduced to fuse multiple signals so as to reduce redundant information. Secondly, a multiscale convolutional module is designed for the feature extraction at different scales by four groups of convolution kernels with different dilate rates. The experimental results on the MET bearing dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the other state-of-the-art deep learning methods in terms of accuracy and antinoise ability.

articleTitle: Lane Detection with the Fusion of CBAM Attention Mechanism and Channel Shuffle Module
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Currently, the main method for detecting lane lines is semantic segmentation. However, there are still some problems with this approach. Firstly, as semantic segmentation requires the extraction of feature information and the classification of all pixels in the vehicle image, lane lines usually represent only a small fraction of the pixels, resulting in a huge computational waste and making it difficult to guarantee real-time lane detection. Furthermore, with semantic segmentation, lane lines can only be distinguished from background information, and it is not possible to form different The lane line instances cannot be formed. Secondly, existing lane detection methods generally have a high false detection rate, making it difficult to ensure the safety of unmanned driving. The safety of unmanned driving is not guaranteed. Therefore, this paper proposes the detection of lane lines using an improved hourglass model to generate key points and incorporates CBAM (Convolutional Attention Mechanism) and channel shuffle modules to further improve detection accuracy and reduce the false detection rate. Firstly, the CBAM attention mechanism is embedded into the encoding-decoding structure to enhance useful features and suppress useless ones. Secondly, the ShuffleNet module is introduced to strengthen cross-channel information exchange between multi-level features at different scales, thus improving the accuracy of recognition for obstructed key points. The model is trained and verified using the TuSimple Lane Line open dataset. Experimental results show that when the model is composed of different numbers of hourglass modules, the proposed lane detection algorithm achieves accuracies of 96.34%, 96.66%, 96.71%, and 96.73%, respectively, verifying the effectiveness of the method proposed in this paper for lane detection, namely, detecting the feasible driving area of lanes.

articleTitle: Pattern Analysis of Transfer Behavior of Public Transit Passengers via Smart Card Data
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Analyzing transfer behavior of public transit passengers is important for improving the public transit system. Using smart card data collected in Shenzhen, China, this paper analyzes the spatial and temporal transfer behavior of public transit passengers from metro to bus. The survival duration model is then used to analyze the time cost for the transfer from metro to bus with investigating the contributing variables including location of the transfer station, passenger flow of the metro station, time when transfer happens, and the type of metro station releasing the transfer passengers. The results show that the above four variables contribute to the time cost of transfer. And the results provide an improved direction of the public transit system.

articleTitle: Research Status and Technological Prospects of Real-Time Path Planning for Tug Collision Avoidance
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In recent years, with the intelligent upgrade of ships and ports, there is increasing attention to the intelligence of tugs. As auxiliary vessels, tugs are responsible for assisting all kinds of ships in berthing, shifting, escorting, and transporting pilots in ports. They are also responsible for social responsibilities such as emergency rescue and firefighting in the port waters, playing a significant role in ensuring port safety. However, the complex working environment, high labor intensity of crew, and high safety risks of tugs make safety collision avoidance and energy consumption issues of paramount importance. Collision avoidance research between vessels has been concentrated on ocean-going ships, and research on tugs has been minimal. Due to the unique characteristics of tugs and their working scenarios, existing collision avoidance theories are impractical. To achieve tug path planning, the development strategy that meets the special characteristics of tugs, improves efficiency, and reduces energy consumption is proposed by analyzing the tug’s uniqueness and working scenarios. The difficult issues of tug path planning are analyzed, and key technologies for achieving tug path planning are demonstrated. It has far-reaching significance for realizing the intelligent upgrading of tugs, constructing smart ports.

articleTitle: Optimization of Bus Routes at Urban Rail Transit Stations Based on Link Growth Probability
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Efficient integration of urban rail lines and buses can improve public transportation. However, current methods for connecting them are not effective or fast. This paper analyzes passenger travel data, including taxi tracks and road network information, to identify potential bus connection stations based on demand. The link growth probability model is then applied to determine the bus lines’ most connected directions based on demand. Finally, a constraint-based exhaustive tree view technique is proposed to speed up the convergence of results. The WEI QU NAN Station in Shaanxi Province is used as an example to evaluate the model’s efficacy. The study reveals 153 prospective stations and lays out the feeder bus network for the entire line, along with a route optimization strategy. Keywords include Feeder Bus, Route Optimization, Link Growth Probability, and Graph Theory.

articleTitle: Spatial-Temporal Characteristics Analysis and Vibration Measurement of Cargo Hold in Bulk Carrier for Cargo Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The main reason for the frequent accidents of bulk carriers with cargoes that may liquefy is that the cargo liquefaction due to many internal and external interference factors. The performance of cargo during marine transportation is significantly affected by the intensity and duration of vibration in the cargo holds in particular. Therefore, it is necessary to find out the relationship between the performance of cargo and the vibration characteristics of the hull. Firstly, the acceleration sensor was arranged at the characteristic position of the whole ship, based on the vibration simultaneous measurement and transmission system, and the vibration data acquisition experiment was carried out by multiple operating modes and ship maneuvering in different marine environments. Next, the vibration data of the internal space of ship hull under different loading conditions were obtained from the simultaneous measurement system, and the time-frequency domain analysis method was used to deal with the instantaneous frequency and amplitude under the time sequence, and an approach to anomaly discernment and risk judgment was proposed. Then, based on the energy transfer function, a method for analyzing the spatial-temporal characteristics of the vibration transfer in the cargo spaces was proposed to carry out the correlation inference between ship operation quality and cargo performance and provide the vibration signal input for the subsequent model experiment of cargoes that may liquefy. The real ship experiment shows that the excitation source and frequency response eigenvalue of the cargo space vibration can be focused, and the spatial and temporal distribution of the vibration response was found. This research has important experimental significance in revealing the coupling effect between cargo performance and ship vibration. It can also provide technical support for cargo performance monitoring and liquefaction situation judgment in the hold of autonomous cargo ships.

articleTitle: Impacts of Connected Automated Vehicles on Urban Parking: A Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Due to limited parking space in metropolitan areas, parking management and design remain a major challenge in urban governance. The emergence and prevalence of connected automated vehicles (CAVs) offer good potential to address this challenge. For example, a CAV can drop off a commuter at the workplace and then autonomously find a parking spot; shoppers in a rush may choose to have a CAV cruise and wait rather than occupy a parking spot. The paper attempts to provide a comprehensive review of how CAVs may reshape parking management/policy, covering three topics: (i) impacts on parking behavior, e.g., parking at home, cruising for parking, etc. (ii) parking policies from the perspective of government and private operators, e.g., demand-side and supply-side strategies; (iii) impacts on parking land use, e.g., need and distribution of parking space, urban layout, etc. A holistic view of CAV parking-related macroscopic models, including bottleneck models, network models, and microscopic models (i.e., agent-based models), is also provided in the paper.

articleTitle: Study on Fire Risk of Pure Car Carrier Vessels Carrying New Energy Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Along with the prosperity of the global new energy vehicle transportation market, the safety problems during the shipping of new energy vehicles begun to appear. Once a fire accident occurs in a new energy vehicle transported by ship, this accident is very difficult to dispose of and the resulting loss will be great. Based on the transport characteristics of those ships, the risk factors that may cause fire accidents in the shipping process are identified, the fire risk evaluation model of the car carrier is established, and the entropy weight TOPSIS method is applied in ranking the risk level of the factors in the model for fire risk assessment. The result shows that in Level 2 indicators, Operator mistake is the most likely cause of ship fire accidents, which means ship personnel management should be strengthened. Besides, in Level 3 indicators, the failure of lithium batteries in new energy vehicles is the most essential factor for car carriers to focus on in their fire accident prevention efforts. The results of this paper can help improve the maritime safety management of car carriers and can also provide some guidance for the risk prevention of fire accidents during the transportation of other ship categories.

articleTitle: Adaptive Choice Behavior of Highway Users in Response to Real-Time Road Accident Information
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: This study aims to investigate the adaptive choice behavior of highway users in response to real-time road accident information. The goal is to provide drivers with driving information that is more tailored to their individual needs. A large-scale SP survey was conducted, which first examined the travel information preferences of 2,500 users and then evaluated their choice behavior in different scenarios, including real-time accident information on highways and alternative road information. The study used latent class analysis to classify the 2,500 users into different clusters and analyzed the choice behavior of each cluster in response to real-time highway information. The study also explored the importance of various feature variables for different clusters using a random forest model and compared it with other machine learning algorithms. The results showed that the random forest model outperformed other models in terms of ROC curve area and accuracy. Finally, to enhance the interpretability of machine learning, the study introduced the SHAP algorithm. The results of the SHAP algorithm showed that different feature factors had significant differences in choice adaptability for different clusters of users, and choice behavior also varied in different scenarios. This study provides practical references for the development of personalized real-time traffic information systems and road traffic safety.

articleTitle: An Autonomous Decision-making Algorithm for Ship Collision Avoidance Based on DDQN with Prioritized Experience Replay
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In order to reduce the influence of human factors on ship collision avoidance, this paper proposes an autonomous collision avoidance decision-making algorithm based on Double Deep Q Network (DDQN) with prioritized experience replay (PER). Based on a full understanding of the International Regulations for Preventing Collision at Sea (COLREGs), and the reward function of the autonomous collision avoidance decision-making algorithm is guided and designed in terms of the number of rudder operations, the amount of the cumulative steering angle during the avoidance process, the DCPA when clear of the other ship, the deviation distance at the end of the avoidance, the total magnitude of ship heading changes during the avoidance process and rule compliance by combining with the statistical results of real water traffic data. Ship encounter scenarios are constructed based on COLREGs, which are arranged and combined the sample training and testing sets for the agent; We compare the algorithm proposed in this paper with DQN, DQN with prioritized experience replay and DDQN algorithms by simulating the same encounter scenario, using this as the training set for the model; Finally, multi-ship encounter scenario simulations are set up as the testing set for the model to verify the performance of the algorithm. The results show that compared with three other reinforcement learning algorithms, DDQN with prioritized experience replay algorithm can make ship collision avoidance decision-making more efficient and improve the safety of ship autonomous navigation under COLREGs; and the trained model can be replicated and applied to a system with any number of agents to provide a reference for ship autonomous collision avoidance research.

articleTitle: Prediction and Mitigation of PM2.5 in Coastal Ports of China
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</inf> has become one of the air pollutants of great concern to achieve green development in coastal ports of China. Accurate prediction will facilitate the prevention and control of PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</inf>. PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</inf> concentrations of 19 coastal ports of China for 2022-2024 were predicted using a seasonal nonlinear Weibull Bernoulli grey model (SWBGM (1,1)) based on monthly data from 2015-2021. A genetic algorithm was used for model parameter optimization. The best simulation outcomes were discovered for Shanghai port, Quanzhou port and Ningbo-Zhoushan port. The prediction results reveal a consistent decline in the annual average PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</inf> concentration for all ports. The PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</inf> concentrations are highest in winter and the lowest in summer, and the monthly distribution follows a U-shape. The predicted PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</inf> concentrations in the Bohai Rim Area are relatively high, particularly in Huanghua port and Tianjin port. Mitigation measures in reducing air pollution were proposed considering the spatial and temporal heterogeneity of the future PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</inf> concentration. The results are expected to deliver effective information for future pollution reduction and sustainable development of the ports.

articleTitle: SE-yolov5 inland waterway vessel target recognition based on CGAN image enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: With the continuous development of deep learning technology, ship target recognition based on video images has emerged as a viable approach for water supervision. However, traditional self-built datasets suffer from insufficient feature sampling and large target recognition errors in ship target detection. In order to enhance the accuracy of ship target detection in complex environments, this paper proposes an improved yolov5 ship target recognition method based on CGAN image enhancement. The method leverages CGAN network to augment the original dataset, thereby completing data enhancement. Furthermore, the SE (Squeeze-and-Excitation) attention mechanism module is integrated into the yolov5 network to train and evaluate the ship image dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that the CGAN network augmentation image outperforms the GAN basic network augmentation image in the dataset, generating type condition constraints. The accuracy of the SE-YOLOV5 network for bulk carriers, container ships, official ships, and beacons is 70%, 97%, 90%, and 60% respectively, showcasing improvements compared to the basic yolov5 network and Faster-RCNN network. The findings indicate that the improved yolov5 ship target recognition method, incorporating CGAN image enhancement, effectively addresses the challenge of low target detection accuracy in multi-target and inland river ships with insufficient lighting conditions under small data sets. It significantly enhances the overall performance of ship detection and recognition.

articleTitle: Distribution Characteristics of water Pollutants Discharged in the Typical Petrochemical Terminal
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Waterborne transportation is known as an important part of the comprehensive transport system, and ports play an important role in the development of shipping and global economic trade. With the continuous increase of the urgency of environmental protection and social concerns, great efforts have been devoted to the promotion of green and sustainable port all over the world. The wastewater generated during the production and operations at Petrochemical terminals has a significant impact on the water quality. The Sinochem Petrochemical Terminal in Quanzhou was selected as the study area. The wastewater monitoring data from January 2020 to June 2023 are utilized to explore the spatial and temporal characteristics. The results show that the wastewater discharge from at the terminal in Quanzhou basically meets the standard, and the annual average compliance rate is approximately 89.32% following one single indicator. In 2020, the number of days exceeding the standard for chemical oxygen demand is 35, accounting for about 9.59%. In 2023, the number decreases to 0. However, the number of days exceeding the standard for ammonia nitrogen increases significantly, with a remarkable increase of 725% between 2020 and 2021. The number of pH exceedances also increases from 1 to 15. More specifically, the rate of exceedance of the standard in December of the same year is higher than in the other months. The variations of water quality parameters can be related to the operational intensity, water temperature at the terminal. More efforts should be made to improve water quality monitor capability, thus effective countermeasures could be taken to ensure environmental protection. The present study could provide a reference to the operations of petrochemical enterprises and the water quality management in the port waters.

articleTitle: Classification of Driving Modes Based on Driving Styles under Natural Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Classification for driving styles is a dominant factor of driving safety in natural scenes. Unluckily, the real-time and multi-dimensional characteristics are always ignored due to the fact that characteristics of vehicle motion parameters are merely focused on any traditional driving style classification. By contrast, the heterogeneities of driving mode characteristics are very remarkable among drivers with different driving styles, which could reflect drivers’ aggressiveness under the natural environment vividly. As such, a corresponding classification method was put forward based on driving modes. Firstly, classification is performed in view of velocity and driving directions. Sub-classification is then carried out in view of those factors such as target states and time headway to gain 18 driving modes. Then, the one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) method is applied to select driving modes which have statistically significant differences between drivers with various styles. Finally, driving styles are classified utilizing the driving cycle multilayer perceptron (DCMLP) integrated with driving modes; also, corresponding training and verification are carried out in combination with driving styles which are calibrated as 3 classes (namely aggressive, common and conservative classes) based on driving data of 44 drivers. Our results indicate that the overall accuracy rate is up to 95.1% for our classification of driving modes whose accurate rates can be above 87%. Aggressive, common and conservative drivers prefer to relative approaching, target-tracking lane change and stable car following, and free lane changing, relative dispersion and free cruising conditions, respectively. The overall accuracy of DCMLP is up to 95.5% which grows by 25.6% compared to those of traditional numerical feature-based classification methods. Our classification method is coupled with traffic environment characteristic parameters so that it can be regarded as a new idea for the classification of driving styles.

articleTitle: Robust Optimization Study of Vessel Formation Departure Scheduling in Three Gorges Lock
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The backlog of vessels in Three Gorges has become the norm. The scheduling of formation sailing according to the vessel crossing plan can improve the efficiency of a vessel crossing to a certain extent. Still, the sailing continuity and the smoothness of the approach channel in front of the dam are directly affected by unexpected events such as temporary vessel control, hydro-meteorological changes, and vessel failure. In this paper, we analyze the characteristics of unforeseen events affecting vessel formation navigation, and construct a robust optimization model for vessel formation navigation dispatching across Three Gorges with the vessel formation arrival time as the uncertain parameter for formation navigation, the minimum idle time at the designated position and the highest execution rate of the lock plan as the objectives, and verify the effectiveness of the robust model through actual vessel navigation data in Three Gorges. The research results show that, compared with the traditional vessel scheduling optimization, the robust optimization model of the Three Gorges Passage Vessel Formation Departure Scheduling proposed in the study avoids delays in lock operation and vessel vacancies caused by uncertainty in vessel sailing time and increases the utilization rate of channel resources by 5.42% and the execution rate of lock times by 12.5%.

articleTitle: Research on Container Throughput Prediction of Chongqing Port Based on Shipping Network
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Port throughput forecasting is an important port development and planning reference index. The container throughput of Chongqing port and its influencing factors are analyzed, and a shipping network-based container throughput forecasting method is proposed. Grey correlation analysis is conducted based on the historical data of container throughput of Chongqing port from 2010 to 2020.BP neural network forecasting method is applied to achieve static forecasts of the container throughput of the Chongqing port. A shipping network centered on Chongqing Port is established based on the container route data of Chongqing Port and surrounding ports. Thus, the dynamic prediction value of the container throughput of Chongqing Port is calculated according to the shipping network circle index. The shipping network-based port container throughput forecasting algorithm could objectively reflect the correction of port throughput by regional development.

articleTitle: Collision Avoidance Path Planning of Open Water Ships Based on Velocity Obstacle Method
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: To solve the problem that velocity obstacle method cannot effectively reflect the safe encounter distance in ship collision avoidance, the ship domain, dynamic boundary, and “Convention on the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea, 1972” are introduced into velocity obstacle method to determine the timing of ships to take collision avoidance actions, avoiding yaw and collision problems caused by early or late collision avoidance. In open water, motion simulation experiments are conducted on two ships in situations including head-on, crossing, overtaking, and emergency, and compared with traditional velocity obstacle method. The results demonstrate that this algorithm can perform collision avoidance behavior more safely compared to traditional VO algorithm. It can maintain minimum safe distance for collision avoidance in different scenarios, which verifies the feasibility of this method for local collision avoidance of ships.

articleTitle: A study on cyclists’ risk-taking behavior intention on shared roads with autonomous vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Automatic vehicles are likely to operate in mixed traffic conditions, affecting cyclists’ existing behavioral decisions. However, the intention and decision-making mechanism of cyclists’ risk-taking behavior on shared roads are not clearly understood. The theory of planned behavior(TPB) has been proven to be effective in the study of travel behavior. Based on the theory of TPB, the Extended Theory of Planned Behavior (ETPB) research framework of risk-taking behavior intention was constructed by introducing safety perception, psychological motivation and technology cognition variables. Safety perception variables took into account the public’s perception of safety in the shared road environment with AVs, while psychological motivation mainly took into account riders’ past riding habits, risk perception bias and riding emotion factors. Secondly, questionnaire survey was used to obtain riders’ personal basic information and multi-situation risk-taking behavior willingness data, and corresponding structural equation model was constructed to explain the influence of variables on willingness. Finally, clustering people by means of K-means clustering algorithm and analyzing the psychological and behavioral characteristics of all kinds of people, so as to facilitate the selection of traffic management strategies. The results show that the extended TPB model can better explain the risk-taking behaviors of cyclists on the self-driving shared road. The influence of attitude and safety perception on the willingness to take risks is more prominent, and technology cognition plays an important indirect role. This study expands the research on the psychology of cyclists’ risk-taking behavior, which could help to promote the integration of autonomous vehicles into transportation systems and better management strategies.

articleTitle: Joint optimization of parcel delivery periodic location-routing and prepositioning disaster response facilities
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce has contributed to the booming distribution demand in rural areas but has also exposed the shortcomings of the lack of terminal facilities. The village-level pickup points (VPPs) and frequency of delivery represent among the most popular solution. In the plateau and mountainous areas where natural disasters are frequent, VPPs have been further advocated should undertake the emergency reserve and rescue function. However, optimally deploying facilities with peacetime and emergency demands remains challenging because of unique demand characteristics. This study presents a joint optimization model to determine the optimal parcel delivery periodic location-routing and prepositioned disaster response facilities location to fill the gap. The model considers the flexible choice of parcel delivery dates and the severity of natural disasters, integrates the objectives of delivery service economy (minimizing cost) and emergency response timeliness (minimizing maximum weighted travel risk). The developed model was applied to an empirical study of a rural township in Qingchuan county, Sichuan, which aimed to demonstrate its effectiveness and replicability. This study will help the plateau and mountainous public sector make informed decisions in assisting parcel delivery network design and rescue resource deployment.

articleTitle: Abnormal driving trace detection method of intelligent vehicles based on alignment analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Road alignment is one of the main factors affecting traffic safety. The vehicle driving trace is the main basis of road alignment design, which has the geometric characteristics of ride comfort, continuous trace curvature, and continuous curvature variation. Since the geometric characteristics of alignment are less considered in the current abnormal driving trace detection methods, a multi-measure fusion method for abnormal driving trace detection of intelligent vehicles was proposed. The three evaluation indexes of curve similarity, ride comfort, and number of consecutive lane changes were integrated to comprehensively evaluate the abnormal driving trace. A piecewise-weighted-average discrete Fréchet distance (PDFD) algorithm was proposed to calculate the curve similarity. This paper analyzed the two dimensions of ride comfort, i.e., the composition of alignment components and the geometric characteristic parameters of alignment components of the driving trace. The five-point orthogonal fitting curvature method was used to extract the alignment components of the driving trace and the segmentation points of each alignment component. According to the principle of orthogonal least squares, the mathematical model of the alignment component of the driving trace was established, and the geometric characteristic parameters were calculated, such as the starting point, end point, radius of the circular curve, center of the circle, starting radius and ending radius of the transition curve, length of alignment components, and curve trend. The experimental results show that the overall accuracy of the abnormal driving trace detection method is 80.4%; the proportion of anomalies caused by the jump of the curvature variation is 41%; the accuracy of the PDFD algorithm is 81%, which is 14% higher than that of the conventional Fréchet distance algorithm of 67%.

articleTitle: Design of VTS radar image-driven ship traffic flow simulation system
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Since the water traffic flow density becomes larger and the navigation environment becomes more complicated in inland waters, which leads to the increase of water traffic accidents, the management problem of water traffic becomes more and more prominent, so a VTS radar image-driven vessel traffic flow simulation system is proposed for the water traffic management in inland waters. Firstly, the general framework of the system is proposed, and the composition and functions of the system are introduced. Secondly, four key technologies introduced in the system are proposed. Since the multi-intelligence approach focuses on describing the behavior of simulation objects, the interaction between simulation objects is better portrayed in the traffic flow simulation system, making the simulation model closer to physical reality, so the multi-intelligence approach is used to construct the traffic flow model. Finally, the application of the system in two aspects, water traffic control and intelligent ship navigation supervision, is proposed, and the conclusions and further research of this paper are prospected.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Bayesian-based Approach for Collision Probability Prediction between Commercial and Fishing Vessels
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: A fuzzy Bayesian network-based prediction approach is proposed, which can be used to estimate the probability between commercial and fishing vessel collisions (CAFV). The kernel of this proposed method is first to collect the collision investigation reports between commercial and fishing vessels, to construct the fault tree between commercial and fishing vessel collisions based on factor analysis, and to use fuzzy sets to quantify the basic events and to calculate their occurrence probabilities. Afterwards, the fault tree is transformed into Bayesian network and the conditional probability table is constructed using Noisy-OR gate. Finally, the model is applied to Rizhao Port, the results are reasonable by comparing the results with the real data. The findings of this paper can provide a reference for reducing the collisions between commercial and fishing vessels.

articleTitle: Overview of Data Management Technology for Transportation Infrastructure based on BIM
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The application of BIM (Building Information Modeling) technology in the field of transportation infrastructure digitization is the current development trend. However, the practical implementation of BIM in transportation infrastructure faces challenges such as inconsistent data standards, low information transfer efficiency, and fragmented information across different life cycles. This paper summarizes the current status and hot spots of BIM data management research through an in-depth literature review, analyzes the problems and shortcomings of existing different forms of BIM data management technology, and a prospect for its future development was proposed in the discussion. The study shows that the file-based BIM data management solutions can hardly meet the BIM data access requests of today’s transportation infrastructure conveniently, securely, and efficiently, and the management solutions based on a single type of database can hardly have good performance while compatible with BIM data of multiple structures due to the heterogeneity of data sources. Therefore, future BIM data management must be based on unified data standards (such as Industry Foundation Classes), combined with NewSql-related technologies to achieve high-performance and highly scalable BIM data management to share and exchange data more conveniently and efficiently.

articleTitle: An Improved VMD-GRU Model for Forecasting the Container Freight Volume of Inland Ports
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Accurate forecasting of container freight volume demand at ports is crucial to the social production and investment decisions of businesses. When dealing with complex, nonlinear fluctuations and ambiguous demand time series, the current methods for forecasting freight volume have demonstrated poor accuracy. In view of this, this study proposes a container freight volume forecasting model using Particle Swarm optimization (PSO)-based Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU). Within the proposed design. In particular, VMD is used to decompose the original time series, which reduces the prediction error caused by disturbances and abrupt changes in the original series. In the meantime, PSO is utilized to optimize the parameter selection of VMD in order to attain the optimal decomposition effect. After decomposition, GRU is utilized to accurately predict each intrinsic mode function (IMF). The final prediction result is obtained by superimposing the predictions of each IMF component. Compared to a BP neural network, a single GRU model, and a support vector machine (SVM), the root mean square error (RMSE), the mean absolute error (MAE), and the mean absolute percent error (MAPE) of the proposed model are smaller, and its prediction accuracy is greater than that of the comparison model.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Coupling Coordination Degree Between Yangpu Port and Qinzhou Port
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Promoting the coordinated development of coastal port clusters is necessary to achieve regional economic and social development, and also provides important impetus for the promotion of major national and regional strategies. This paper takes Yangpu Port and Qinzhou Port, two important port nodes of the New western land-sea corridor, as the research objects, constructs a port coupling coordination degree model, and analyzes the coordinated development status and trend of the two ports by measuring and predicting the coupling coordination degree of Yangpu Port and Qinzhou Port from 2014 to 2021. The results show that according to the current development status, the two ports can reach the coupled coordination status of high quality coordination by 2025, and the Yangpu Port contributes slightly more to the coordinated development of the combined system of the two ports. Based on the analysis of the current development situation of the southwest coastal ports, the article also puts forward suggestions for the coordinated development of the two ports and the mutual promotion of the regional economy.

articleTitle: Multi-dimensional solar energy utilization potential assessment method for port
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The photovoltaic industry is developing rapidly and has become one of the main means of utilizing solar energy resources. As the huge amount of solar energy resources, the photovoltaic system can accelerate the green transformation of the port. In this paper, based on the characteristics of solar resource endowment of port and considering the construction factors of photovoltaic system, the assessment method for the photovoltaic system in port is proposed. Specifically, different photovoltaic utilization coefficients are assigned to the land types of ports, and the numerical model of photovoltaic panel is built. Then, the photovoltaic potential assessment model of the port is obtained. The feasibility of the construction of photovoltaic system in port is obtained by considering economy and carbon emission reduction. Finally, the reasonableness and feasibility of the proposed method are verified through the suitability assessment of photovoltaic system in Ningbo-Zhoushan Port. In 17 years, the PV power generation potential of Ningbo-Zhoushan Port is 68550.07 GWh, the net present value is 36.118 billion yuan, and the carbon reduction emission is 38.6×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> t, which provides a port scheme for the “carbon peaking and carbon neutrality” goals.

articleTitle: Collision Risk Hotspot Identification Based on AIS Data and DBSCAN Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The objective of the present study is to identify ship near-miss areas and identify the hotspot waters with higher collision risks. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) data from the waters near Zhoushan Island is used in the study. The ship trajectory is interpolated to extract near-misses between ships based on data at the same time. Then, risk modeling is carried out based on the relative parameters between the encountered ships. Finally, the near misses are clustered using DBSCAN (Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise) algorithm. The degree of collision risk is quantified using Collision Risk Index (CRI) models, which is also involved in the DBSCAN algorithm. The results describe the distribution of collision risky sites in the waters near Zhoushan Island. The research results can be used for safe navigation of ships and the development of near classified maps to prevent collisions between passing ships, for deck personnel to take preventive measures when passing through hazardous areas.

articleTitle: A Fuzzy Logic-Based Model for Evaluating Grounding Risk of Inland River Ships
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Grounding is the main type of accidents in inland river water traffic. Based on the statistics data of water traffic accidents, this research carries out the cause analysis of Grounding accidents, and builds the risk warning model of ship Grounding accidents. The early warning indicators of grounding accidents include visibility, excess water depth, wind force and ship deviation from the channel. On the basis of this, the weights of early warning indicators affecting accident risk are determined by analytic hierarchy process, and the early warning risk levels are divided into three levels: low risk, medium risk and high risk by triangular fuzzy number. The scientificity and applicability of the proposed model are verified by the case study on ships in Yueyang area of Yangtze River.

articleTitle: Feature and cause analysis of global ship contact accidents by using DEMATEL-AR
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: With the development of large-scale ships and the shipping industry, ship contact accidents also occur occasionally. In order to enhance navigational safety and control the risks from contact accidents, it is necessary to investigate the characteristics of global ship contact accidents and in-depth analysis of their causes. This paper focuses on the feature and cause analysis of contract accidents by incorporating the decision-making trial and evaluation laboratory (DEMATEL) and association rules (AR) based on global ship contact accidents from 1977 to 2022. First, the contact accident data are dealt with regarding involved ships, accident severity, and spatial and temporal distribution of contact accidents, and a frequency matrix of contact accidents is proposed. Second, a co-occurrence network model is proposed to identify the critical features of contact accidents. Third, the frequency matrix is further processed as the complex network’s input matrix using the DEMATEL method and AR. Furthermore, the complex network of influencing factors of ship contact accidents is used to identify the relevant factors affecting the severity of ship contact accidents and pollution degree. Then, the centrality of the complex network is analyzed to obtain the critical factors affecting the severity of ship contact accidents and pollution degree. The research results can provide theoretical support for risk management of contact accidents.

articleTitle: A study of the Architecture Design of digital software for Transportation Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The digital software of transportation infrastructure is the foundation of digital transportation. With the development of information technology, its software technology architecture is also evolving iteratively. Based on the status quo in the field of transportation infrastructure engineering, the core basic capabilities of the software are determined, including data aggregation and storage, data analysis and processing, engineering data delivery, engineering visualization, system integration expansion, application customization development, etc. The characteristics of the existing software architecture are studied, and the logical architecture of the transport infrastructure data software system is designed, including operation support layer, convergence storage layer, data service layer, and application service layer. In addition, the technical reference architecture and operation architecture of digital software for transport infrastructure are emphatically introduced, and the development trend of digital software architecture for transport infrastructure has been prospected.

articleTitle: Research Status and Technological Prospects of Scenario Generation Methods for Ship Collision Avoidance Tests
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: This paper presents a review of the current research on scene generation methods, focusing on ship collision avoidance testing. By analyzing the simulation methods of collision avoidance models and algorithms from domestic and foreign research, a virtual scene generation method based on international maritime collision regulations and AIS ship data is proposed. Furthermore, this paper discusses the emerging research trends and the challenges that need to be considered in the validation of autonomous collision avoidance testing of ships. Additionally, this paper introduces the concept of automated intelligent ships, their various levels, and the relevant policies and plans of the Chinese government for the development of intelligent ships.

articleTitle: Characterization of Wave Features Based on Momentum Sources of Sphere Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Wave is one of the most prevalent physical phenomena within the vast expanse of the ocean. The simulation of Wave holds significant importance within the realm of hydrodynamics. In this manuscript, a numerical wave tank model is formulated, employing the concept of spherical structures as a source of momentum. This model serves to simulate the processes of wave generation and absorption within the numerical wave tank. Furthermore, a distinct procedure is established for the superimposition of waves, utilizing the dual momentum sources offered by the spherical structure model. Experimental endeavors are conducted to create waves based on the aforementioned momentum source, aiming to validate the rationality of the numerical outcomes. The results reveal that the average amplitude of waves after superimposition is roughly twice that of the initial state, while the distribution of wave frequencies remains unaltered throughout the superimposition process. It is confirmed that the waves generated by the dual momentum source of the spherical structure adhere to the principle of wave superimposition, corroborating the findings of numerical simulations. Consequently, this method of wave generation furnishes insights for simulating wave conditions under natural marine circumstances.

articleTitle: Overview of Ship Navigation Conflicts in Complex Waters
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The increase in ship traffic density in coastal waters leads to difficulties in ship navigation and a rise in the number of navigation accidents. To further understand the navigation conflict risk in complex waters, the methods of ship navigation risk are compared and summarized in this paper by reviewing previous studies. Sum up the main challenges and development trends of navigation conflicts research as follows: 1) the difficulties of establishing a dynamic quantitative model of ship navigation conflict in complex water remaining; 2) the dynamic and reliable conflicts assessing on a global scale will be a central trend in future research work.

articleTitle: A multi-source matching model for static data of ships in Chongqing
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The estimation of ship CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions based on high-frequency Automatic Identification System (AIS) data, serves as a crucial reference and prerequisite to attain the emission reduction target within the shipping industry in Chongqing. Nevertheless, precise estimation of ship CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions depends on detailed vessel information, which may not always be readily available in the vessel parameter database. This challenge is particularly pronounced in inland watersheds, where a substantial amount of static ship data is missing. This study addresses this issue by utilizing a sample database comprising information from 2857 ships passing through or mooring in the Chongqing water area. Regression fitting, graded filling, and regional modularization are combined to construct a multi-source matching model, which could be deployed to supplement the missing static ship data within the study area. The regression fitting technique establishes the relationship between a ship’s dimension, and its main engine power. The graded filling technique is used to discover the relationship between a ship’s length and its main engine power, as well as its length and design speed. The regional modularization technique is utilized to find the relationship between a ship’s location information and its main engine power, as well as its location information and design speed. By employing these multiple methods, the success rate of data matching is improved, consequently enhancing the practicality and reliability of the model. The multi-source matching model for static ship data effectively fills the gaps within the static ship database in Chongqing and resolves the challenge of calculating ship CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions within the region.

articleTitle: OceanCL-IDS: A Continual Learning-based Intrusion Detection System for Ocean-going Ship-Satellite Communication Network
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Deep learning-based intrusion detection has become an effective approach to ensure the security of communication network traffic in scenarios such as the Internet of Things (IoT) and the Internet of Vehicles (IoV). However, there is relatively little research on intrusion detection for ship-satellite communication network in marine scenarios. In addition, due to the inherent catastrophic forgetting issue of deep learning models, vanilla intrusion detection methods can only recognize previously learnt attack types, but cannot learn new attack types in real time. In this paper, an ocean-going ship-satellite communication network (OSSCN) intrusion detection system (OceanCL-IDS) is proposed, which can effectively alleviate the communication interference caused by the harsh maritime communication environment. Furthermore, a continual learning algorithm GEM based on replay strategy is introduced into the system, which is capable of continual learning new attack features while retaining the capacity to detect previously learnt attack. Finally, to validate the efficacy of the proposed methods, a dataset with attack labels and maritime communication features is constructed by collecting long-term satellite network traffic data of real ocean-going ships. Extensive experimental evidence demonstrates that our method successfully beats existing continual learning algorithms on a variety of metrics.

articleTitle: Application of Big Data Technology in Standardized Operation Management of Urban Rail Transit
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In order to promote the safe and orderly operation of urban rail transit, it is required to strengthen the comprehensive analysis of various operation data of urban rail transit. This paper studies the application of big data technology in urban rail transit operation, proposes to build a hybrid architecture platform of Green Plum and Hadoop, and conducts research at the levels of data source, data collection, data analysis and mining, real-time analysis and query, data storage, auxiliary decision-making, data exploration, and human-computer interaction to analyze the implementation effect of big data platform in urban rail transit operation. It significantly improves the intelligent management level of urban rail transportation and meets the demand of standardized operation of stations.

articleTitle: A study on Autonomous Vehicles’ Driving Behavior Based on Open Road Test Data
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In this paper, the Autonomous Vehicles (AVs)’ actual driving performance in open road test and its impacts on traffic were studied. We used free flow speed, minimum headway, maximum acceleration and deceleration as characteristic parameters for AVs’ driving behavior. And based on the matching results of trajectory data and road network, the above parameters were extracted. The analysis of the above characteristic parameters showed that the values of the free flow speed, minimum headway, and maximum acceleration and deceleration of AVs in the test cannot be expected better than the corresponding values of Human-Driven Vehicles (HVs) like many previous relevant studies did. Actually, according to the extracted values and dispersions of the behavior parameters, the AVs even perform worse than HVs. As a result, the expected significant improvements in the operational efficiency and safety of the traffic causing by AVs did not occur according to the simulation. There were even signs of deterioration. The results of this paper will help people re-examine the behavior parameter settings of AVs in study and provide reference for enterprises and governments to improve the behavior of AVs from the perspective of traffic system efficiency and safety.

articleTitle: Analysis of Factors Influencing the Severity of Heavy and Medium Truck Traffic Accidents
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: With the development of China’s economy, heavy and medium-sized trucks are playing an increasingly important role in the transportation of bulk materials on main highways and supporting major national engineering construction. But the risk of road traffic accidents caused by it has also become increasingly prominent. This article takes the accident data of heavy and medium-sized trucks in recent years as an example, and based on the ordered Logit algorithm, analyzes the high influencing factors of the severity of heavy and medium-sized truck accidents. Then, the accident severity prediction model based on random forest algorithm is constructed to predict the accident. Research has shown that the high impact factors on the severity of heavy and medium-sized truck accidents are road type, road surface conditions, lighting, vehicle type, driving experience, accident responsibility, driving status, and traffic control methods. The research conclusions can provide decision-making reference for the prevention of heavy and medium-sized truck accidents.

articleTitle: Analyzing Traffic Conflict Risk at Diverge Area of Left Off-Ramp of Underground Interchanges Using Multinomial Logistic Regression
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In order to deeply analyze the traffic conflict risk and the significant influencing factors of conflict risk at the diverging area of the left off-ramp of underground interchanges, this study classifies the conflict risk into three levels: no-conflict risk, general conflict risk, and severe conflict risk, and uses SPSS software to design orthogonal experiments on independent variables and obtain 16 groups of practical solutions, and simulates the experiments by VISSIM microsimulation software, and finally obtains 16916 groups of experimental data and constructs a multinomial disorderly Logit traffic conflict risk model from four aspects, such as the length of the deceleration lane, the traffic volumes of the mainline, the traffic volumes of the ramp and the design speed of the mainline. The results show that, 1) with no-conflict risk as the base group, the four categorical independent variables have a significant effect on both general conflict risk and severe conflict risk when vehicles are driving within the left exit diversion area; 2) when the length of the deceleration lane increases from 120m to 145m and other variables are fixed, the logarithm of the occurrence ratio of the conflict risk of vehicles in the general conflict risk and the no-conflict risk decreases by 0.112; 3) when the traffic volumes of the mainline increases from 5000pcu/h to 5900pcu/h and other variables are fixed, the logarithm of the occurrence ratio of the conflict risk of vehicles in the severe conflict risk and the no-conflict risk increases by 1.192; 4) when the traffic volumes of the ramp increases from 600pcu/h to 650pcu/h and other variables are fixed, the logarithm of the occurrence ratio of the conflict risk of vehicles in the severe conflict risk and the no-conflict risk increase by 1.192; 5) when the design speed of the mainline increases from 50km/h to 70km/h and other variables are fixed, the logarithm of the occurrence ratio of the conflict risk of vehicles in the severe conflict risk and the no-conflict risk increases by 1.679.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Multi-Layered and Time-Dependent Congestion Control Strategy for Mixed Traffic Flow
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: This paper proposed a comprehensive multilayered and time-dependent congestion control strategy for the coexistence of connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) and human-driven vehicles in future mixed traffic systems. A linear programming model was developed with the objective of minimizing the average travel time. A genetic algorithm was used to optimize the time taken by CAVs to enter the main road via the entrance ramp, resulting in an optimal control strategy that satisfies the objective function and constraints. Typical scenarios with three different origin-destination (OD) distribution types were designed and the effectiveness of the control strategy was demonstrated through primary simulation analysis. In an approximately uniform distribution of OD scenario, 23 CAVs (representing 2.71% of all vehicles) were controlled but were able to reduce the average travel time of the entire mixed traffic system by almost 55%. Significantly improving the efficiency of the traffic system and alleviating the prevalent spatiotemporal congestion problem. Furthermore, in two scenarios with a ununiform OD distribution, by controlling CAVs that account for no more than 5% of all vehicles, it was possible to exceed the average travel time by 70% and 25% respectively. Overall, this study confirmed the effectiveness of the proposed congestion control strategy, which achieved significant control results at a relatively low cost. It showed great promise for further testing and application in traffic management.

articleTitle: Hybrid Intersection with Pre-signal: An Innovative Approach to Increase Intersection Capacity
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Exclusive left-turn phases are often adopted to ensure the safety and efficiency of left-turn movements in conventional intersection signal timing schedules. Due to the need for at least two exclusive left-turn green phases for four-way intersections, some approach lanes for left vehicles are spare during the green phase, resulting in intersection capacity drop. To fix this drawback, we propose a hybrid intersection strategy based on pre-signal and sorting areas in this study. The ad hoc traffic flow control method of the hybrid intersection reduces the number of exclusive left-turn phases from at least two, in conventional four-way intersection conditions, to only one. Furthermore, sorting areas charge pre-organized vehicles during green pre-signals and discharge vehicles during green intersection signals, so that the hybrid intersection can be used for as many approach lanes as possible to discharge vehicles during the green intersection signals. Considering traffic demand, lane allocation, and signal schedule, we construct binary mixed-integer linear programming (BMILP) to formulate the capacity maximization problem of the hybrid intersections. A series of case studies show that, the hybrid intersection strategy can achieve higher capacity significantly than other pre-signal strategies and conventional roundabout. In addition, the hybrid intersection strategy can achieve optimal capacity when demand of left-turn vehicles (LVs) and through vehicles (TVs) are huge and relatively close, and when the cycle length is moderate (around 70s).

articleTitle: Ship-Based Carbon Capture of LNG Ships Under Off-Design Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The carbon capture process model was established for an LNG ship, and the solution concentration and flow rate analysis selection under design conditions were carried out. The effect of solution flow rate on the carbon capture rate, energy and other key factors in the carbon capture system under off-design conditions was studied, and further research on the exhaust gas treatment mass flow and solution flow rate control was conducted under 75% MCR conditions. The results of the study showed that the energy of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> regeneration and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> removal rate increased significantly with the decrease of main engine load. The solution flow rate at the optimum operating point decreases approximately linearly with decreasing main engine load, while the optimal liquid-to-gas ratio (molar) does not tend to change with changing main engine load, so the solution flow rate can be controlled approximately linearly to achieve the optimum capture operating conditions when the main engine load changes. The appropriate exhaust gas treatment mass flow and solution flow rate can help to further reduce the regeneration energy based on the high CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> removal rate. Up to 82.8% CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> removal rate can be achieved at the regeneration energy of 9.477 GJ/T CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> under 75% MCR condition. This study can provide a reference for the control of carbon capture effect under off-design conditions of ships.

articleTitle: Investigating the Influencing Factors of Vehicles’ Lateral Position Stability on Expressway
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
